data.title: Error notification closes, and leaves on its own
data.body:
GitHub issue #2.

## Goal
A notification of a failed action (a refused move, a cycle in links, a write error) no longer
stays until some later action succeeds: it has a × that closes it, it fades out by itself after
a few seconds, it stays while the pointer is over it, and a new one replaces it and starts the
time again.

## Approach
- Model: the notice becomes a `Notice` (text, a sequence number, when it was shown, held or
  not, leaving since when) behind one setter, `Model::warn`, which every place that sets it today
  (about 20, in model.rs, activity.rs, graph.rs, palette.rs and the view's persist) goes through.
  A new notice always gets a new number and a fresh time, even with the same text. `notice()`
  reads it; `dismiss_notice()` closes it; `hold_notice(bool)` holds it while hovered, and letting
  go starts its time again.
- Timing lives in the model, tested with injected instants: `age_notice(now, fade)` starts it
  leaving `NOTICE_FOR` (6 s) after it was shown, unless held, and drops it `fade` later. Holding
  it while leaving brings it back. A successful action still clears it, as now.
- View: the notice gets a × (Boxicons `x`) and an `on_hover` that holds it; while leaving it fades
  out with an animation keyed by its number, so a replacement starts fresh. The poll repaints only
  when the notice changes.

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/model.rs, model/{activity,graph,palette}.rs, src/ui/mod.rs,
src/ui/icons.rs, tests/{model,links,ui}.rs.

## Acceptance check
- `cargo test -p livtk-app`: model tests show a notice leaving after its time and gone after the
  fade, a held one staying, letting go restarting its time, and a new one replacing the old with a
  fresh time; a UI test closes it with its × and another keeps it while hovered.
- `scripts/check` passes.
- In the app: a refused drag shows the notice; it goes after about 6 s, stays while hovered,
  and the × closes it.

data.title: View options menu: show empty groups, show dismissed work
data.body:
GitHub issue #1.

## Goal
In the list views (Tasks, Lessons, Decisions, Findings), the dock's eye button becomes a View
options button that opens a menu upwards, as Grouping and Ordering do, with "Show empty groups"
and "Show dismissed work" (H). Each view remembers both between runs. The Graph keeps its eye
button as it is (decided: no groups or filtering on the graph yet).

## Approach
- Model: `Display` (per view) gains `show_empty` and `show_dismissed`; the app-wide
  `Model::show_all` goes. H, the palette and the graph's eye toggle the current view's
  `show_dismissed`; the palette's reveal shows dismissed work in the view it reveals in.
- `arrange` lists, with show_empty on and a grouping, every group of the grouping in its usual
  order (each state of the view's kind by rank, or priorities 1 to 4) with a count of 0 where
  empty; dismissed states only while show_dismissed is on. Off, as now. Collapsing and dropping
  onto an empty band work as on any band.
- The board keeps every column either way (`columns`), reading the view's show_dismissed.
- Saved: `SavedView` gains `show_empty` and `show_dismissed`. The old app-wide `show_all` is still
  read once from an existing app.toml, so nobody's setting is lost, and no longer written.
- View: the `Menu::View` popover with two checkbox rows (H shown on the second), a dock button
  (Boxicons `slider-alt`, "View" when wide), highlighted while open or while an option is on.
- Palette: "Show/Hide empty groups" beside the dismissed toggle, in the list views.

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/model.rs, model/{saved,palette,graph}.rs, src/ui/mod.rs, src/ui/icons.rs,
tests/{model,saved,palette,graph,ui}.rs, README.md.

## Acceptance check
- `cargo test -p livtk-app`: model tests for empty groups (state and priority, order, count 0,
  dismissed only when shown, collapsed, the board unchanged), per-view settings, and the saved
  round trip including the old show_all; UI tests that the menu opens upwards from the dock and
  toggles both, and that H still toggles.
- `scripts/check` passes.
- In the app: Tasks → View options → Show empty groups lists every state band, Review with 0.

data.title: Port the app to macOS: Cmd shortcuts and a native titlebar
data.body:
## Goal
On macOS the app feels native: shortcuts use Cmd where other platforms use Ctrl (Cmd+K for the
palette, Cmd+B for the sidebar, Cmd+Enter to create, Cmd+? for the shortcuts), every place that
names a shortcut shows the Mac's keys (⌘ K), and the window has the native traffic-light buttons
on the left, in a titlebar merged into the app, above the sidebar's project name.

## Approach
- Keys: bind with GPUI's `secondary-` modifier (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) instead of `ctrl-`
  for the app's own shortcuts. Ctrl+N/Ctrl+P in the palette stay Ctrl, as on every Mac text field.
  Check what the textarea reports for Cmd+Enter (today Ctrl+Enter arrives as a secondary Enter).
- Labels: one helper names the modifier for the platform ("⌘" on macOS, "Ctrl" elsewhere) and
  every label goes through it: the shortcuts modal, tooltips, the palette's shortcuts, the
  sidebar's hint, the form's "Ctrl ↵". The palette's labels live in the model, so the helper is
  GPU-free and tested there.
- Graph: zoom with Cmd+scroll and the trackpad's pinch on macOS, as Ctrl+scroll elsewhere.
- Titlebar: on macOS, `TitlebarOptions { appears_transparent: true, traffic_light_position }`,
  so the content runs to the window's top; the sidebar (and the rail) leave room at the top for
  the traffic lights, and that strip drags the window (a window-drag area). Other platforms
  unchanged.
- Measure first: what gpui-pre 0.3.9 offers for each (secondary bindings, transparent titlebar,
  traffic-light position, window dragging) before building on it.

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/ui/mod.rs, src/model/palette.rs, possibly a small `ui/platform.rs`,
tests/{ui,palette}.rs, README.md (shortcut table per platform).

## Acceptance check
- On this Mac: Cmd+K opens the palette, Cmd+B collapses the sidebar, Cmd+Enter creates a task,
  Cmd+? shows the shortcuts; Ctrl+K does nothing.
- Every shortcut label in the app reads ⌘ on macOS.
- The traffic lights sit at the top left over the sidebar, nothing overlaps them, in the
  sidebar and in the rail, and dragging the strip moves the window.
- UI tests pass on macOS with the platform's keys; `scripts/check` passes.

data.text: Found while checking TAS-1: tests/ui.rs a_double_click_edits_the_title_and_esc_cancels fails on macOS before any change. It selects all with ctrl-a, which on macOS moves to the line start ("renamed planfirst"); select-all there is cmd-a. The UI tests need the platform's keys too.

Built as planned. Beyond the plan: (1) tick() runs every 200 ms, so a failure that lasts (an unreadable log) would have been re-told on every tick, restarting its time and bringing it back after a close; each project now remembers its failure and it is told once, when it begins or changes (test: a_failure_that_lasts_is_told_once_not_on_every_tick). (2) The notice's element id is stable and a replacement keeps the hold, so a pointer over the old notice still holds the new one; animations are keyed per notice. (3) crates/livtk-cli/tests/hooks.rs ran hooks from the crate's directory, which became a livtk project when this repo was initialised; hooks now run from the temp dir. Checks: fmt, clippy, all tests pass; two failures predate this work: the macOS ctrl-a UI test (noted on TAS-3) and the ignored memory test with_a_missing_model_search_falls_back_to_keywords, which needs the model but escapes scripts/check's --skip with_model filter by its name.

review: UPHELD (1) cargo test -p livtk-app (debug, skipping the macOS ctrl-a test): all pass. Model tests in tests/model.rs cover a notice leaving at NOTICE_FOR and gone after the fade, a held one staying, letting go restarting its time, being held while leaving bringing it back, a new one with the same text getting a new id and a fresh time, and a lasting tick failure told once. UI tests the_notice_closes_with_its_x (clicks notice-close, model and element gone) and the_notice_stays_while_the_pointer_is_over_it (real pointer move -> on_hover -> hold) pass. Every place that set the notice now goes through warn (grep: only warn/dismiss/age/run-success write it). / REFUTED (2) scripts/check does not pass as written: it stops at 'tests: the app' on a_double_click_edits_the_title_and_esc_cancels, and with that skipped the ignored step fails on livtk-core memory.rs:456 with_a_missing_model_search_falls_back_to_keywords, which needs LIVTK_TEST_MODELS and escapes --skip with_model. I confirmed with git stash that the ctrl-a failure predates the change, and the memory test is in livtk-core, which the change does not touch. fmt, clippy, cargo deny, core+CLI tests and the app's ignored tests pass, so nothing here is caused by this change, but the point as stated is not met. / UNVERIFIABLE (3) a refused drag in the app: drop_on -> run -> warn path is correct in code; settle it by running the app, dragging to a refused column, and watching for about 6 s, hovering, and clicking the x. Minor, outside the check: after the 240 ms fade the card stays at opacity 0 and still occludes clicks until the next 200 ms poll removes it (ui/mod.rs:4207 occlude, model.rs:887 removes it only on a tick, so up to about 160 ms), and hovering it in that window brings it back. A replacement inherits held (model.rs:853), so a smaller new card under a still pointer stays held until the pointer moves.

After review: (1) scripts/check now passes on this Mac. The two failures it found predate TAS-1: the title-editing UI test selected all with ctrl-a, which on macOS moves to the line start, now secondary-a (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere); and two model tests (with_a_missing_model..., search_by_meaning_of_10k...) lacked the with_model_ prefix the script's --skip relies on, now renamed with_model_gone_search_falls_back_to_keywords and with_model_search_by_meaning_of_10k_nodes_per_keystroke. (2) A faded notice stood unseen for up to a poll (200 ms), taking clicks; a one-shot timer now takes it away when its fade ends (end_notice_fade). Kept as designed: a replacement under a still pointer stays held until the pointer next moves.
The ctrl-a UI test was fixed under TAS-1 (secondary-a).

review 2: UPHELD (1) cargo test -p livtk-app (debug): model tests pass (a_notice_leaves_on_its_own_after_its_time_and_a_fade, ..._stays_and_gets_its_whole_time_again_when_let_go, a_new_notice_replaces_the_old_and_starts_its_time_again, a_notice_closes_and_a_success_clears_it, a_failure_that_lasts_is_told_once_not_on_every_tick) and UI tests the_notice_closes_with_its_x and the_notice_stays_while_the_pointer_is_over_it pass. (2) scripts/check exits 0 here: fmt, clippy, core+CLI, app with UI tests (debug), ignored benchmarks. Caveats: cargo-deny is not installed in this environment so the supply-chain step was skipped (the change touches no Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock), and there is no model dir, so with_model tests were skipped. (3) Issue: the x removes it (UI test), it fades after NOTICE_FOR and hovering holds it, a test covers both. Same error repeated gets a new id and a fresh time. The one-shot end_notice_fade timer is a no-op if the notice was replaced or held during the fade. GPUI 0.3.9 on_hover also fires on MouseExit and on layout changes under a still pointer, so a held replacement is let go once it is no longer under the pointer. (4) The renames keep their meaning: bodies and #[ignore] are unchanged, they still run with LIVTK_TEST_MODELS and are now caught by --skip with_model. secondary-a is Cmd-A on macOS and Ctrl-A elsewhere, and the exact title assertion still proves select-all replaced the text. / REFUTED (5) A lasting catch-up failure is told again on every cycle. model.rs:826 caught_up calls warn with no per-project memory. ui/mod.rs:515-517 then ticks right away, and the tick finds the store still stale and queues the next job, which fails too. Every cycle makes a new id and a fresh time: the notice never fades, a close with the x is undone within one catch-up, and the fade-in replays each time. Shown by a scratch probe (read-only .livtk dir, log rewritten): ids 1,2,3,4 on four cycles, and a dismiss is followed by a new notice. (6) A failure in a background tick is not painted when it is told. tick() warns (model.rs:785) but returns false, and the poll at ui/mod.rs:428 notifies only on changed||busy||aged, with no check for a new notice. The same goes for a persist() failure (ui/mod.rs:1808). A scratch UI probe (unreadable log, three 200 ms polls) found the notice in the model but not drawn. It was first drawn about 6 s later, when it began to leave, so the human sees it only as it fades out. The plan said the poll repaints when the notice changes. / UNVERIFIABLE (7) In the app, a refused drag: the code path drop_on -> warn is user-driven and repaints. Settle it by running livtk-app, dragging a card to a refused column, waiting about 6 s, hovering, and clicking x. Minor, from reading the code: on_hover is InputModalityAware, so a key press with the pointer resting on the notice lets it go on the next paint, and it can fade under the pointer.

After review 2: (1) a catch-up that kept failing was told again on each try: caught_up warned with no memory, and the tick's stale branch cleared the memory. Project::went is now the one rule for both tick and caught_up (a failure is told when it begins or changes), and a stale tick leaves the last catch-up's failure standing (test: a_catch_up_that_keeps_failing_is_told_once). (2) A notice raised by the poll (tick, persist) was not painted until it began to leave: the poll now repaints whenever the notice's id or leaving changed across it (test: a_failure_found_by_the_poll_shows_at_once). Both tests were seen to fail with their fix taken out. scripts/check passes (cargo-deny not installed).

data.title: Catch-up retries without pause while it keeps failing
data.body:
Found while doing TAS-1.

## Goal
A catch-up that fails (a read-only store, a held lock) is retried with a growing pause, not at
once over and over.

## What happens now
`LivtkApp::run_catch_ups` (crates/livtk-app/src/ui/mod.rs) ticks as soon as a job ends; the tick
finds the store still stale and queues the next job, which fails as fast, so a lasting failure
loops on the background executor without rest. Since TAS-1 it is told once, so the loop is
silent, but it still spends CPU and disk.

## Approach (to plan)
Back off per project after a failed catch-up (say 1 s doubling to 30 s), reset on success; the
model holds when the next try may start, tested with injected instants.

data.text: review 3: UPHELD (1) cargo test -p livtk-app (debug) passes, 70 UI tests included. The model tests cover a notice leaving at NOTICE_FOR and gone after the fade, a held one staying, letting go restarting its time, a new one (same text too) replacing the old with a new id and a fresh time, a lasting tick failure told once, and a catch-up that keeps failing told once. UI tests the_notice_closes_with_its_x and the_notice_stays_while_the_pointer_is_over_it pass. (2) scripts/check exits 0: fmt, clippy, core+CLI, the app with UI tests (debug), ignored benchmarks. cargo-deny is not installed and there is no model dir, so those steps were skipped; the change touches no Cargo files. (3) Background paths: the poll compares (id, leaving) before tick and after persist and repaints on a change, and the caught_up path always notifies. Scratch UI probes in a copy of the repo show a poll-found failure drawn on that poll, not told again after a close while it lasts, and told again with a new id when it clears and returns. Replaced while hovered stays held. Closed while hovered, then a new notice under the still pointer: held, because GPUI re-checks hover on layout. end_notice_fade does nothing if the notice was replaced or held during the fade. Notices are global, so a project switch changes nothing. / REFUTED (4) Issue point 'hovering it keeps it' fails after a key press. The notice's on_hover (ui/mod.rs:4231) uses GPUI's default HoverListenerMode::InputModalityAware, which reports not hovered after any key press (gpui-pre 0.3.9 test default_hover_listener_ends_after_key_press). hold_notice(false) (model.rs:873-880) then lets it go and restarts its time, so it fades out under a pointer that never moved. Probe: hover the notice, press Down, redraw; age_notice(now + 2*NOTICE_FOR) returns true with the pointer still at the notice's centre. Fix: .hover_listener_mode(HoverListenerMode::InputModalityIndependent). / UNVERIFIABLE (5) In the app, a refused drag shows the notice, it goes after about 6 s, stays while hovered, and the x closes it. The real-clock path (poll age_notice, then the end_notice_fade timer) has no end-to-end test because the tests drive age_notice with injected instants. Settle it by running livtk-app, dragging a card to a refused column, waiting about 7 s without touching anything, then hovering for longer than 6 s, then clicking x.

After review 3: a key pressed with the pointer resting on the notice let it go (GPUI's on_hover is input-modality aware by default), so it faded under a still pointer. The notice's hover listener is now InputModalityIndependent; the_notice_stays_while_the_pointer_is_over_it presses a key while hovering and was seen to fail without the fix. scripts/check passes.

review 4: UPHELD (1) The fix from review 3: the notice's on_hover (ui/mod.rs:4233-4237) is set to HoverListenerMode::InputModalityIndependent. In gpui-pre 0.3.9 that mode uses hitbox.id.is_hovered_ignoring_last_input, a plain hit test that ignores the last input's modality (div.rs:1754-1758, window.rs:799). The test the_notice_stays_while_the_pointer_is_over_it presses j with the pointer on the notice, redraws, and checks that it is still held. In a scratch copy, removing that one line made the test fail at tests/ui.rs:2515 ('still held after a key press'), so the test catches the bug. Scratch probes with the fix: the pointer stayed on the notice through j, k, down, up, escape, shift, cmd, g, enter and escape, with two redraws after each key; every time it was still drawn under the pointer, held, and not leaving. A replacement shown after a key press under a still pointer was held. After a close, a key press and a new notice under the still pointer, the new one was held too. (2) cargo test -p livtk-app (debug): the model tests a_notice_leaves_on_its_own_after_its_time_and_a_fade, a_notice_under_the_pointer_stays_and_gets_its_whole_time_again_when_let_go, a_new_notice_replaces_the_old_and_starts_its_time_again, a_notice_closes_and_a_success_clears_it, a_failure_that_lasts_is_told_once_not_on_every_tick and a_catch_up_that_keeps_failing_is_told_once all pass. So do the UI tests the_notice_closes_with_its_x, the_notice_stays_while_the_pointer_is_over_it and a_failure_found_by_the_poll_shows_at_once. (3) scripts/check exits 0: format, lint, core and CLI tests, the app with its UI tests (debug), and the ignored benchmarks (quick and release). cargo-deny is not installed here, so the supply-chain step was skipped; the change touches no Cargo files. There is no model directory, so the with_model tests were skipped. (4) Issue #2's acceptance: the x removes the notice (UI test). It fades out after NOTICE_FOR (6 s), and hovering keeps it, now including after key presses (model and UI tests). Tests cover both. A new notice gets a new id and a fresh time. The only code that sets the notice is warn, dismiss_notice, age_notice and the success paths that clear it (model.rs:695, 726). / REFUTED none. / UNVERIFIABLE (5) In the app: a refused drag shows the notice, it goes after about 6 s, stays while hovered and the x closes it. The real-clock path (the 200 ms poll calls age_notice, then the end_notice_fade timer) has no end-to-end test, because the tests use injected instants. To settle it, run livtk-app, drag a card to a refused column, then wait about 7 s without touching anything. Make it fail again, hover it for more than 6 s and press a few keys without moving the mouse, then click the x. Cosmetic, from the code: hovering a notice while it fades replays its fade-in from 0 opacity (ui/mod.rs, notice-in-{id}).

After review 4 (nothing refuted): its cosmetic point fixed. A notice caught while fading played its fade-in again from nothing, as the fade-in was drawn only while not leaving and GPUI forgot it had played. The fade-in now sits on an outer wrapper drawn throughout (once per notice), the fade-out on the card inside, so a caught notice returns at full strength. Visual only, so no headless test; scripts/check passes.
hey
Checked in the app by the developer: the notice leaves after its time, stays while hovered and through key presses, comes back whole when caught fading, and closes with its ×.

data.title: The rewritten-log tick budget fails on macOS
data.body:
Found while checking TAS-2; fails on main too.

## What happens
crates/livtk-app/tests/model.rs a_rewritten_log_of_100k_events_never_stalls_the_tick (an ignored
benchmark that scripts/check runs) asserts the first tick after git rewrites a 100k-event log
takes under 1 ms. On this Mac it takes 1.1 to 1.4 ms (4 runs in 5 fail); on the developer's
Linux machine it was 84 µs.

## Measured
`Workspace::stale()` on that store: 36 to 90 µs settled; the first call after the 30 MB log is
rewritten 1.18 ms, the next ones 35 to 55 µs. So it is the file system's first touch of a file
just written (APFS), not livtk's code; the replay the tick avoids takes 770 ms, the poll is
200 ms.

## Decision needed (developer)
The budget is the developer's. Options: keep 1 ms and accept it fails on macOS; a budget per
platform; or a budget that says what "never stalls" means here (well under a frame, say 5 ms).

data.text: Built as planned. Display gains show_empty and show_dismissed (per view, saved; the old app-wide show_all is read once from app.toml and never written). arrange lists every group of the grouping with show_empty: each state of the view's kind in display order (dismissed only when shown) or priorities 1-4, empty ones with 0; ungrouped and the inbox have none. The board keeps its columns. H, the palette and the graph's eye act on the current view; the palette's reveal shows dismissed work in the view it opens. Dock: View options (slider-alt, 'View' when wide) with a menu of two checkbox rows that stays open; the graph keeps its eye. Palette: Show/Hide empty groups in the lists. README updated. Tests: model (state and priority groups, order, counts, dismissed, per view, filter, collapse, board), saved (round trip, the old show_all), palette, UI (menu opens upwards, toggles, H). scripts/check: all green except the macOS tick budget (TAS-5), which fails on main too.

review: UPHELD: cargo test -p livtk-app passes (debug, UI tests included); the model tests cover empty groups by state and priority, their order, count 0, dismissed states only when shown, collapsed, the board unchanged, and per-view settings; saved tests cover the round trip and the old show_all; the UI test shows the View menu opening upwards from the dock (menu.bottom <= button.top), toggling both options, and H still toggling. scripts/check exits 0: format, lint, all tests, and the quick/release benchmarks, including ten_thousand_tasks_stay_fast (TAS-5's tick benchmark also passed on this run). Probes in a scratch copy (tests/probe.rs) also pass: Lessons/Decisions/Findings grouped by state, priority and none with every empty/dismissed combination keep groups contiguous and unduplicated, with dismissed states only when shown; a filter that matches nothing leaves every band at 0; dropping on an empty state band, a collapsed empty band and an empty priority band moves the row; j/k step over empty bands; the board's columns are the same with empty groups on or off; H and the empty toggle are no-ops in the Inbox and Activity and leave Tasks' setting alone; an old app.toml with show_all = true and a [views.tasks] lacking the new keys restores dismissed work in every list and the graph; a new app.toml is written without show_all and reads back each view's own show_empty/show_dismissed. Observation, not a defect against the issue: with show_empty on and no matching rows, the list shows 0-count bands instead of the 'No tasks here' message. / REFUTED: none. / UNVERIFIABLE: In the app, Tasks > View options > Show empty groups lists every state band with Review at 0. data.title: List or Board moves into View options; Shift+H shows empty groups
data.body:
Asked by the developer after trying TAS-2.

## Goal
The dock gets lighter: List or Board is chosen at the top of the View options menu, above a
single separator and the two checkboxes, instead of by tabs in the dock. Keys: `h` shows or hides
dismissed work (as now), `Shift+H` shows or hides empty groups.

## Approach
- View options menu (Tasks): a Layout part at the top, List and Board as a pick-one pair (the
  chosen one ticked, as Grouping's rows are, `B` shown), one `menu_divider`, then "Show empty
  groups" (`Shift H`) and "Show dismissed work" (`H`). Choosing a layout leaves the menu open,
  as the checkboxes do, so the whole display is set in one visit. Lessons, Decisions and
  Findings have no layout: their menu starts at the checkboxes, with no separator.
- The dock's List/Board tabs (`dock_layout`) go; the View button stays where it is. Its label
  when wide stays "View".
- Keys: bind `shift-h` in the list area to a new `ToggleEmpty` action calling
  `Model::toggle_empty`; `h` stays `ToggleAll`. Check GPUI reports Shift+H as `shift-h`
  (not `H`) so the binding matches, with a UI test that presses it.
- Labels: the menu rows, the palette's "Show/Hide empty groups" (shortcut `Shift H`), the
  shortcuts modal (Display: H dismissed work, Shift H empty groups), README's key table and dock
  description.
- Tests: UI (the dock no longer holds the tabs; the menu has Layout first, a separator, then the
  options; choosing Board from it switches and keeps the menu open; `b` still toggles; `h` and
  `shift-h` toggle their options), palette label, style test untouched.

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/ui/mod.rs, src/model/palette.rs, tests/{ui,palette}.rs, README.md.

## Acceptance check
- `scripts/check` passes (TAS-5's macOS budget aside).
- In the app, Tasks: the dock has no List/Board tabs; View opens with List / Board ticked as
  chosen, a line, then the two checkboxes; choosing Board shows the board. `h` toggles dismissed
  work, `Shift+H` empty groups.

data.title: Add system notification to the inbox

data.text: Built as planned. The dock's List/Board tabs (dock_layout) are gone; View options for Tasks starts with List and Board (icon, label, B on the one it would switch to, a tick on the chosen), one divider, then Show empty groups (Shift H) and Show dismissed work (H); a choice leaves the menu open. Other lists: options alone, no divider. Model::set_layout added. Keys: shift-h -> ToggleEmpty in the list area; h unchanged; the UI test shows shift-h does not also fire h. Shortcuts modal, palette shortcut and README updated. scripts/check passes.

data.title: Show empty groups hides or shows the board's empty columns
data.body:
Asked by the developer after trying TAS-6: on the board, Show empty groups did nothing.

Decided (developer, in chat): it works on the board as in Linear. Off hides the columns with no
cards; on shows every column. This reverses issue #1's "The board keeps every column either
way". Moving a card to a hidden state stays possible from its state icon's menu, not by
dragging. The option is off by default, so the board starts without its empty columns.

## Approach
- `Model::columns` keeps its working order (backlog to done, then parked and canceled while
  dismissed work is shown, or priorities 1 to 4) and, with `show_empty` off, leaves out the
  columns with no cards after filtering. One rule for list and board: what `show_empty` says.
- The board with no columns at all (nothing matches, or no tasks) shows the empty state the
  list shows, rather than a blank area.
- The View options menu says nothing new: the same checkbox now acts on both.
- Tests: model (board columns off: only those with cards, in order; on: every column; a filter
  emptying one hides it when off; dismissed columns only when shown), UI (toggling on the board
  adds and removes column elements; the empty board shows its message). Board tests that drag
  onto an empty column turn empty groups on first, as a human would.
- README: Show empty groups covers the board's columns too.

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/model.rs, src/ui/mod.rs, tests/{model,ui}.rs, README.md.

## Acceptance check
- `scripts/check` passes (TAS-5's macOS budget aside).
- In the app, Tasks as a board: with Show empty groups off only columns holding cards show;
  Shift+H brings every column back; a card moves to a hidden state from its state icon.

data.body:
Asked by the developer (title only); this plan is Claude's reading of it, for the developer to
confirm by acknowledging.

## Goal
When something new waits for you (Claude planned a task for your acknowledgement, proposed a
lesson or decision) and the app's window is not in front, the system shows a notification:
"TAS-12 waits for your acknowledgement: <title>", or "3 things wait for you" when several come at
once. Clicking it brings the app forward with the Inbox open on that item.

## Measured first (2026-10-16)
GPUI 0.3.9 has system notifications (`App::show_system_notification`, a tag that replaces, a
response callback), through macOS's UNUserNotificationCenter. macOS allows them only to an app
bundle: GPUI turns them off with a log line for a bare binary, which is what `cargo install`
installs. So the app needs a bundle to notify.

## Approach
- Model: `tick` already knows when the inbox changes; it also records what newly entered the
  inbox from anyone but the human (by node id, so an item is told once), for the view to take.
- View: after a tick, if new items arrived and the window is not active, post one notification
  with a fixed tag (`livtk-inbox`, so they never pile up): one item named, or a count. On a
  response: activate the window, go to the Inbox, select the item.
- Bundle: `scripts/bundle-app` builds `target/livtk.app` (Info.plist with a bundle identifier,
  the release binary, the icon if one exists) and `scripts/check --install` copies it to
  `~/Applications/livtk.app`; `livtk-app` from the shell keeps working, without notifications.
- Linux: GPUI's own notifications where it has them; nothing breaks where it has none.
- Tests: model (new inbox items from Claude are reported once; the human's own are not; a burst
  is one report), UI (no notification while the window is active; one when not, through a test
  platform hook if GPUI's test platform records them, else the model's report).

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/model.rs, src/ui/mod.rs, scripts/bundle-app (new), scripts/check, README.md.

## Acceptance check
- `scripts/check` passes (TAS-5 aside).
- From ~/Applications/livtk.app with the window in the background, `livtk new x && livtk move
  TAS-n planned` from a terminal shows a notification within a second; clicking it opens the
  Inbox on TAS-n. With the window in front, nothing is posted.

Asked by the developer (title only); this plan is Claude's reading of it, for the developer to
confirm by acknowledging.

## Goal
The Filter menu (`/`) narrows a list by state as it does by priority: a State part under the
priorities, with a checkbox per state of the view's kind; checked states only are shown.

## Approach
- `Display` gains `states: Vec<State>` (empty: every state), per view and saved in app.toml as
  the priorities are. `arrange` keeps only rows in a checked state.
- The menu: a "State" heading and one row per state of the view's kind, each with its state mark
  and name, in display order; dismissed states listed only while dismissed work is shown.
  "Clear filters" clears them too; the Filter button's count counts them.
- With Show empty groups on, a group of an unchecked state is not listed: the filter says what
  the view is about. On the board likewise for columns.
- The Inbox mixes kinds and keeps its filter as now (title and priority).
- Tests: model (filtering by states, with priorities and text; empty groups respect it; per
  view; saved round trip), UI (the menu lists the kind's states, a click filters, clear clears).

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/model.rs, model/saved.rs, src/ui/mod.rs, tests/{model,saved,ui}.rs,
README.md.

## Acceptance check
- `scripts/check` passes (TAS-5 aside).
- In the app, Tasks: Filter → State → Planned shows only planned tasks; the button says Filter · 1;
  Clear filters brings everything back.

Found while checking TAS-2; fails on main too.

## What happens
crates/livtk-app/tests/model.rs a_rewritten_log_of_100k_events_never_stalls_the_tick (an ignored
benchmark that scripts/check runs) asserts the first tick after git rewrites a 100k-event log
takes under 1 ms. On this Mac it takes 1.1 to 1.4 ms and fails about one run in two; on the
developer's Linux machine it was 84 µs.

## Measured
`Workspace::stale()` on that store: 36 to 90 µs settled; the first call after the 30 MB log is
rewritten 1.18 ms, the next ones 35 to 55 µs. It is the file system's first touch of a file just
written (APFS), not livtk's code. The replay the tick avoids takes 770 ms; the poll is 200 ms.

## Plan (Claude's recommendation; acknowledging it is the decision)
The test exists to show the tick never stalls the window, so its budget says that: under 5 ms,
well inside one 16 ms frame and 150 times under the replay, on any platform. One budget, no
per-platform branch. The comment above it records the measurements of both machines. The plan's
section 21 measurement stays as it was (Linux, 84 µs) with this one added.

Not chosen: keeping 1 ms (the check fails on macOS by chance); a budget per platform (two numbers
for one claim).

## Files
crates/livtk-app/tests/model.rs, docs/plan.md.

## Acceptance check
- The benchmark passes ten runs in a row on this Mac in the quick profile.
- `scripts/check` passes end to end.

Built: each project keeps, after a failed catch-up, when the next may start and the pause that led there: 1 s (RETRY_FIRST), doubling to 30 s (RETRY_MAX). A tick finding the store stale before that time starts nothing; a catch-up that works, or a store found current, resets it. Model::tick_at(now) beside tick() so tests drive time. Test a_failed_catch_up_is_tried_again_after_a_pause_that_grows (8 failures, the cap, the reset; seen failing without the pause); a_catch_up_that_keeps_failing_is_told_once steps past the pauses. scripts/check passes.

GPUI Component's textarea reports secondary-enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS). Elsewhere unchanged (TITLEBAR = 0). review: UPHELD goal: a failed catch-up sets per-project next_try (1 s doubling, clamped to 30 s; pause*2 and now+pause cannot overflow under the cap); tick_at skips a stale project before next_try (model.rs:818) and the 200 ms poll retries once it passes, so run_catch_ups' tick right after a failed job queues nothing. A success (caught_up Ok) or a store found current, including one caught up by another process (Ok(Some) -> try_now), resets it. Pauses are per Project, so other projects are not held, and select_project only changes current. While it waits catching_up stays false and the failure stands without being told again (continue skips went), so TAS-1's told-once rule holds. scripts/check passes in full; the probe tests for two projects, a reset by another process and the short pause again all pass. REFUTED 'tested with injected instants': caught_up stamps the pause with Instant::now() (model.rs:882, try_later) rather than an injected time, so the new test a_failed_catch_up_is_tried_again_after_a_pause_that_grows depends on the wall clock. Its 'nor before its pause' check, tries(pause - 50ms), fails if more than 50 ms passes between caught_up and that tick (one stale() disk read in between). Probe: sleeping 60 ms there makes the same assertion fail. It is flaky under load, but the product behaviour is right. Fix: caught_up_at(job, result, now), or a margin tied to the clock. UNVERIFIABLE: none.

After review (one point refuted: the test read the real clock between caught_up and its ticks, so it could fail on a busy machine): Model::caught_up_at(job, result, now) beside caught_up, as tick_at beside tick; the test now runs on its own clock, each failure at the moment of its retry, ticks 1 ms before and at the pause's end. Seen failing without the pause; 3 runs pass; scripts/check passes end to end.

Built as planned: TICK_BUDGET = 5 ms with the measurements of both machines above it; docs/plan.md section 21 records the macOS figure and why. The benchmark passed 10 of 10 runs in the quick profile, even with two reviewers compiling. scripts/check: format, lint and every test pass; the CLI's list benchmark failed only while two reviewers ran full checks at once (core and CLI tests took 48 s instead of 7), to be rerun quiet.

Display.states (per view, display order, saved by name; names of other kinds or unknown are dropped on restore). arrange keeps rows in a chosen state; with Show empty groups only the chosen states get bands, and the board only their columns. Filter menu: a State part under Priority (checkbox, state mark, name), dismissed states only while dismissed work is shown; the button counts it; Clear filters (now Model::clear_filters) clears it; the palette's reveal clears it too. review 2: UPHELD goal: a failed catch-up sets a per-project pause (try_later, model.rs:231: 1 s doubling, clamped to 30 s); tick_at skips a stale project before next_try (model.rs:819), so run_catch_ups' tick right after a failed job (ui/mod.rs:536-537) queues nothing and the 200 ms poll retries once it is due; a success (model.rs:887) or a store found current (model.rs:833) resets it. data.body:
Asked by the developer (title only); this plan is Claude's reading of it, for the developer to
confirm by acknowledging.

## Goal
Esc in a text field takes the keys back to the list (or board, feed, graph): the field loses
focus, so j/k, a, n and the rest work again at once. Today this holds everywhere but the detail
panel's note field ("Leave a note…"), where Esc does nothing and the keys stay in the field.

## Approach
- One rule at the window's root rather than one per field: an Esc (GPUI Component's
  `input::Escape`) that no deeper handler took gives the focus back to the list area. The fields
  that already do more on Esc keep it, as GPUI stops an action at the first handler: the filter
  closes its menu, the title and body editors cancel, the palette, the form and the shortcuts
  close. A field added later is covered without a line of its own.
- The note's draft stays in the field, as Linear keeps one; a second Esc, now in the list, closes
  the detail panel as it always has.
- Tests (UI): in the note field, Esc gives the keys back (j moves the selection, the draft is
  kept, nothing typed ran a command); a second Esc closes the panel; the filter, the editors and
  the palette keep their own Esc.

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/ui/mod.rs, tests/ui.rs.

## Acceptance check
- `scripts/check` passes.
- In the app: open a task, click the note field, type, Esc, then j: the selection moves and the
  draft is still in the field.

data.text: Diagnosis of the developer's note (no notification when an item arrived): the running app (pid 70074, started 19:07 local) is ~/.cargo/bin/livtk-app launched from a shell, not ~/Applications/livtk.app. macOS allows notifications only for an app bundle, and GPUI turns them off for a bare binary, quietly; macOS has no notification entry for com.github.nebulaw.livtk, so it never asked for permission. Since the bundle was installed, the only arrivals from Claude were TAS-10 moved to planned (14:59 UTC) and LES-2 proposed (15:11 UTC); the developer's own moves are not news by design. The defect that stands: the app one naturally runs has no notifications and says nothing about it.

Decided (developer, in chat): on macOS, livtk-app run from a shell hands off to the bundle when it is installed (opens ~/Applications/livtk.app with the same arguments and exits); LIVTK_APP_HERE=1 keeps the bare binary for development; without the bundle it runs as now and tells once how to get notifications.

Built the developer's decision: crates/livtk-app/src/launch.rs (GPU-free): in_bundle(exe) tells a bundle by its path (.app/Contents/MacOS); bundle_to_open picks ~/Applications/livtk.app, else /Applications/livtk.app, unless LIVTK_APP_HERE is set or it runs from a bundle; open_bundle runs 'open -a <bundle> --args <projects>' with absolute project roots (the bundle starts elsewhere). main: on macOS a bare livtk-app hands off and exits when that works; else it runs and the model tells once ever (saved in app.toml as told_no_notifications) that no notifications come from there and where they do. Tests: launch.rs (bundle paths; home first, then all users, none, LIVTK_APP_HERE, never itself), model where_no_notifications_come_the_human_is_told_once_ever (also across a restart). README updated. scripts/check passes. Installed ~/.cargo/bin/livtk-app and ~/Applications/livtk.app (19:16). Waiting for the developer's live check.

data.title: macOS app experience: menu bar, Cmd+W hides, Cmd+Q quits, Dock menu
data.body:
Asked by the developer; scope agreed in chat (2026-10-17): Cmd+W keeps the app running so
notifications continue, Cmd+Q quits; the menu bar as proposed.

## Goal
livtk behaves as a Mac app: a full menu bar whose items are the app's own commands (so menu,
keys and palette never disagree), Cmd+W hides the window while the app keeps watching and
notifying, a Dock click brings it back, Cmd+Q quits, and a Dock menu. Designed so the menu model
is platform-neutral (Windows and Linux get their own presentation later).

## Measured first (gpui-pre 0.3.9)
`set_menus`, `set_dock_menu`, `MenuItem::{action, os_action, submenu, os_submenu, separator}`,
`OsAction` (undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select all), `hide`, `hide_other_apps`, `quit`,
`on_reopen`, `on_window_should_close`, `minimize_window`; on macOS the default QuitMode is
Explicit, so the app does not quit when its window closes. Menu items show the key bindings of
their actions; macOS disables an item whose action no focused handler takes.

## Approach
- Menus (`ui/menus.rs`, one table): livtk (About livtk, Check for Updates… [after the updater],
  Services, Hide Cmd+H, Hide Others Opt+Cmd+H, Show All, Quit Cmd+Q); File (New Task Cmd+N, Open
  Project… Cmd+O, Projects ›, Close Window Cmd+W); Edit (system Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste,
  Select All, wired to the text fields' own actions); View (Inbox … Graph Cmd+1…Cmd+7, List or
  Board, Show Empty Groups, Show Dismissed, Toggle Sidebar Cmd+B, Command Palette Cmd+K, zoom);
  Task (Acknowledge/Ratify/Accept, Ratify as Standing Rule, Reject, Priority ›, Add Note, Add
  Link…); Window (Minimize Cmd+M, Zoom, Bring All to Front); Help (Keyboard Shortcuts, livtk on
  GitHub, Report an Issue).
- Every item dispatches an existing action; new ones only where none exists (Close Window, Quit,
  About, the views by number). The model's legality rules decide what an action does; macOS greys
  an item no handler takes.
- Cmd+W: the window refuses to close and the app hides (window, model, poll and notifications stay
  alive); a Dock click or opening the app again shows it (`on_reopen`). Cmd+Q quits (writing
  app.toml first). Other platforms keep closing as now.
- About livtk: a small modal with the version (and the build number, once TAS-b1 adds it).
- Dock menu: New Task, Inbox (with its count, refreshed when it changes), the projects.
- The shortcuts modal, README and plan list the new keys.

## Files
crates/livtk-app/src/ui/{mod,menus}.rs, tests/{ui,style}.rs, README.md, docs/plan.md.

## Acceptance check
- `scripts/check` passes; UI tests: Cmd+W hides and keeps polling (a change arriving while hidden
  notifies), reopen shows it, Cmd+1..7 switch views, Cmd+N opens the form, Edit items reach text
  fields, the menu table only names actions that exist.
- In the app: the menu bar is complete; Cmd+W, a Dock click, Cmd+Q, Hide, Minimize do what a Mac
  app does; the Dock menu works.

data.title: Updater: update the app bundle and relaunch, from a local source now
data.body:
Asked by the developer; scope agreed in chat (2026-10-17): "Restart to Update", never on its own;
the CLI inside the bundle; macOS first, designed for Windows and Linux.

A parent task: its parts are planned and acknowledged on their own.

## Goal
livtk updates itself: it finds a newer build, prepares it quietly, offers "Restart to Update",
swaps the installed app atomically and relaunches where you were; a failed start rolls back.
What never changes is the contract (a versioned manifest and a small installer step); where
updates come from is the part meant to change (a local folder now, an HTTPS feed later).

## Parts
1. Build identity, and one bundle holding the app, the CLI and the updater helper.
2. The updater: manifest, local source, staging and verification, the macOS installer with
   rollback, "Restart to Update", and a release script that fills the local source.

data.title: One bundle: build identity, and livtk inside livtk.app
data.body:
Part 1 of TAS-15. Agreed in chat (2026-10-17): the CLI ships inside the bundle, so one update
covers the app, the CLI and the hooks. It also settles TAS-7's last review: the handoff guessed a
build's age from file times and a development build from a folder named target.

## Goal
Every livtk binary knows exactly which build it is, and on macOS the app and the CLI are one
installed thing: ~/Applications/livtk.app holds livtk-app and livtk, and the commands on PATH
are links into it. The handoff stops guessing.

## Approach
- Build identity, in livtk-core (`build::{VERSION, BUILD, COMMIT, MODIFIED}`), made by a build
  script from git: BUILD the number of commits on HEAD (monotonic on main), COMMIT its short
  hash, MODIFIED whether the tree had changes; outside a git checkout BUILD is 0. `livtk
  --version` and `livtk-app --version` print "livtk 0.4.0 (build 87, abc1234)", with
  ", modified" when it was. The app's About (TAS-14) shows it.
- The bundle: Contents/MacOS holds livtk-app and livtk; Info.plist carries CFBundleVersion =
  BUILD, CFBundleShortVersionString = VERSION, and LivtkCommit. `scripts/bundle-app` builds
  both.
- The command line tool: `livtk-app --install-cli` (and, with TAS-14, the menu item "Install
  Command Line Tool") links ~/.local/bin/livtk and ~/.local/bin/livtk-app into the installed
  bundle, says if ~/.local/bin is not on PATH, and names any older livtk earlier on PATH (a
  cargo-installed copy in ~/.cargo/bin) with how to remove it. `scripts/check --install` on
  macOS installs the bundle and the links instead of cargo-installing the binaries; elsewhere it
  stays `cargo install`.
- The handoff, simplified: `livtk-app` started through a link that resolves into a bundle opens
  that bundle (so a shell returns at once) and exits; started inside a bundle by macOS it runs;
  anything else (a development build, cargo's own copy, Linux, Windows) runs as itself. The file-
  time and folder-name heuristics go, with their notices: the Stale case no longer exists. The
  one-time "no notifications from here" notice stays for a bare binary on macOS.
- Hooks: Claude Code runs `livtk` from PATH, so through the link it runs the bundle's CLI: one
  version for the app, the CLI and the hooks.

## Files
crates/livtk-core/{build.rs,src/build.rs,src/lib.rs}, crates/livtk-cli/src/main.rs,
crates/livtk-app/src/{main.rs,launch.rs,model.rs}, scripts/{bundle-app,check}, tests,
README.md, docs/plan.md.

## Acceptance check
- `scripts/check` passes; tests: the identity is set and ordered; --version prints it; the
  handoff decision from invoked and resolved paths (link into a bundle opens it; inside a bundle
  runs; a target/ build or a plain copy runs); install-cli links, reports PATH and shadowing, and
  is idempotent (temp HOME).
- On this Mac: after `scripts/check --install`, `which livtk` is ~/.local/bin/livtk, a link into
  ~/Applications/livtk.app; `livtk --version` and the app's About agree; `livtk-app` from a shell
  opens the bundle and returns; the old ~/.cargo/bin copies are named for removal.

data.title: The updater: find, verify, stage, Restart to Update, swap and roll back
data.body:
Part 2 of TAS-15. Agreed in chat (2026-10-17): "Restart to Update", never on its own; a local
source now, another later; macOS implemented, Windows and Linux designed for.

## Goal
The app finds a newer build of itself, prepares it in the background, offers "Restart to
Update", and on that quits, swaps the installed bundle atomically and relaunches where you were;
if the new build does not start, the old one comes back. Nothing in the contract changes when the
source or the platform does.

## The contract (what never changes)
- Manifest, JSON, `"format": 1`: app, version, build, commit, platform (macos, windows, linux),
  arch (aarch64, x86_64), artifact (a path relative to the manifest, or later a URL), sha256,
  size, notes, and a reserved `signature`. Readers ignore fields they do not know, so a newer
  manifest never breaks an older app; a newer `format` is skipped, never misread.
- Ordering by build number (TAS-16), never by file time.
- The installer step is a small separate program inside the bundle, `livtk-update`, with a fixed
  command line: wait for a pid to exit, move the installed app aside, move the staged one in
  (one volume, so each move is atomic), relaunch, and restore the old one if the new one does not
  report a healthy start in time. It has no network code and never will.

## Approach
- `livtk-core::update` (GPU-free): Manifest parse and validate; `Source` trait with
  `LocalFolder` (on macOS ~/Library/Application Support/livtk/updates/, from
  `scripts/release`); `stage` (copy, verify size and sha256, unpack with ditto on macOS, check the
  bundle's identifier and build match the manifest); `Installer` trait with the macOS one; others
  answer Unsupported, which the app shows as "an update is available" without installing.
- The app: checks at launch, every 6 hours and from "Check for Updates…" (TAS-14's menu);
  stages in the background; then "Restart to Update" in the livtk menu and a quiet line in the
  sidebar's footer, never a modal. On it: save app.toml, start livtk-update, quit. The relaunched
  app, on a healthy start, marks it so; after an update it says once what changed (the notes).
- `scripts/release`: builds the bundle, zips it (ditto), writes the manifest with sha256 into the
  local source. The signature stays reserved until updates leave this machine (then ed25519 with
  a key built into the app).
- The app log records each check, stage, install and rollback.

## Files
crates/livtk-core/src/update/*, crates/livtk-update (new, tiny), crates/livtk-app/src/{ui,
model}, scripts/{release,bundle-app}, tests, README.md, docs/plan.md.

## Acceptance check
- `scripts/check` passes; tests: manifests (good, unknown fields, newer format, wrong platform,
  bad hash, wrong identifier or build); the local source picks the newest build for this platform;
  the installer's swap and rollback in a temp folder (a start that never reports healthy restores
  the old app); the app shows Restart to Update once staged.
- On this Mac: install build N, `scripts/release` build N+1, the app offers Restart to Update,
  restarting runs N+1 where you were; a deliberately broken N+2 rolls back to N+1.

data.text: Its last two defects (build age from file times, development build from a folder named target) move to TAS-16, which replaces the guess with a compiled-in build identity and the CLI in the bundle; what TAS-7 delivered is done and was checked live.

Deviation from the plan, decided before building: the identity lives in a tiny crate of its own, livtk-build (build script + constants), not in livtk-core. It changes with each commit; in core it would rebuild everything that depends on core each time, in its own crate only the binaries that print it.

review 2: the per-node draft fix is UPHELD everywhere it was probed, but one REFUTED point remains (pre-existing, not introduced by the fix). Probe UI tests ran on a copy. UPHELD: (1) j/k: the draft stays on LIV-1; LIV-2's field is empty; k brings it back with the caret at the end; typing goes on and Enter posts 'one two' on LIV-1 only. (2) A row click: LIV-2 is empty, LIV-1 gets its draft back; the click blurs the field and the keys still work. (3) Palette jump to LIV-2: empty, Enter adds nothing, LIV-1's draft comes back. (4) Feed (event clicks) and graph (card clicks): each node keeps its own draft, and Enter posts on the right node. (5) Closing by Esc Esc or by close-detail clears the field and parks the draft. Reopening the same node, or c from the closed list, brings it back. Another node opens empty. note_drafts drains to 0. (6) Project switch with ]: B's LIV-1 is empty and Enter adds nothing. Back in A, LIV-1's draft is there and posts in A only. (7) Enter after a switch: j c enter, with no frame between, posts nothing on LIV-2 (headless). (8) A whitespace-only draft is kept as typed. Enter posts nothing (add_note trims) and clears it. (9) Swapped while focused (c onto another node, or a background rename): focus stays, the caret sits at the end, typing appends. Undo cannot reach another node's text (set_value clears the undo history). (10) The first review's Esc points all still hold. Title and body editors: Esc cancels, saves nothing, the panel stays, j moves. Link picker and palette: they close, no link is added. The filter closes its menu. The note field: the panel stays and j moves; a second Esc closes the panel. New-task form, title and body after Tab: it closes and nothing is created. The shortcuts close. Without track_note the shipped test and probe_jk fail, so the fix is what makes them pass. REFUTED: Claude moves the open node to a dismissed state while the human types its note. Path: j, Enter on LIV-2, c, type 'for two'; Claude moves LIV-2 to canceled; the poll runs; Enter. The panel still shows LIV-2 with its draft and focus, but the note lands on LIV-1. Cause: reload reselects rows.first() (model.rs:1392-1393) while the detail stays on LIV-2, and on_note (ui/mod.rs:718) calls add_note, which goes through acted_on (model.rs:594-597), and acted_on prefers the selection over the detail's node. The base without track_note does the same, so the fix did not cause this. Still, 'Enter posts the draft on its own node' is false here. Fix: post the note on model.detail's node, not acted_on. scripts/check passed end to end (format, lint, every test with UI, core/app and CLI release benchmarks) with no timing failure; load average 4.86 before the run, 16.72/85.81/61.91 after. cargo-deny is not installed, so the supply chain is UNVERIFIABLE here.

After review 2 (refuted, a bug older than TAS-10: when a change from elsewhere moved the selection off the node open in the panel, Enter in its note field posted on the selected row instead): Model::add_note posts on the panel's node, whose field it is; without a panel, on the node acted on, as before. Test a_note_goes_to_the_node_open_in_the_panel_even_when_the_selection_moved (Claude cancels the open task; the note lands on it, not on the row selected after), seen failing with the old rule.

review 3: the latest fix is UPHELD for every caller of add_note, with two REFUTED edges and one minor pre-existing gap. Probe UI tests ran on a copy (accessors added there only). UPHELD: (1) Enter in the note field (on_note, ui/mod.rs:718): Claude cancels LIV-2 while it is open; the selection falls to LIV-1, and the note lands on LIV-2, the panel's node. (2) c with the panel closed opens the selected row and posts there. The palette's Add a note with the panel closed opens the selected row (its label says LIV-1) and posts on LIV-1. (3) The feed (no row selected): c opens the highlighted event's node and posts there. After Esc j moves the highlight, the panel stays and the note goes to the panel's node. (4) Project switch: select_project clears the panel (model.rs:505-517). After ], j c in B posts in B only. A cancel by Claude in B while the panel is open posts on B's open node. ] c Enter without a frame posts nothing in B. (5) Every review 2 probe still passes, including each field's Esc (title, body, link picker, palette, filter, note, new-task form and its body, shortcuts) and per-node drafts (j/k, clicks, palette, feed, graph, close and reopen, whitespace, focused swap). REFUTED (a), introduced by this fix: the palette label disagrees with where the note goes. With the panel on LIV-2 and the selection on LIV-1 (the cancel path above), Ctrl+K shows 'Add a note' with context LIV-1, because node_actions uses acted_on (model/palette.rs:376). Running it posts on LIV-2. Before the fix, label and post agreed (both LIV-1). Fix: give the palette's Add a note (and Edit title or description, which also act on the panel) the panel's node as context, or make acted_on prefer the panel. REFUTED (b), from track_note (review 1's fix): drafts are keyed by node id only (note_drafts: HashMap<Uuid,String>, ui/mod.rs:387, track_note :3782). Two open projects that share ids, such as a copy or a second clone with the same .livtk, share drafts. Type 'for a' in A's LIV-1, Esc, ], c: B's LIV-1 panel shows 'for a', and Enter posts it in B. Fix: key drafts by (project, id). Minor, pre-existing (base 1504213 has the same Note action): c in the graph with no card selected opens no panel but focuses the hidden note field. Keys type into it until Esc, which the new root handler now rescues, and the text is later dropped. scripts/check: format, lint, all tests (UI included) pass. Benchmarks failed under load: the app's a_frame_of_a_thousand_node_graph_stays_in_budget took 16.7 ms against a 16 ms budget, then passed 3/3 alone and in the full core/app step twice. The CLI list_of_10k_tasks_stays_under_10ms_warm took 20-21 ms in the full step three times, then passed alone at load 19.8. Load average: 16.59 at start, 41.58/50.50/44.99 at the failure, 17.01/29.81/37.03 at the end. Other rustc builds were running. cargo-deny is not installed, so the supply chain is UNVERIFIABLE.

review (refuter, copy at 1504213 + ALL-9.patch): NOT accepted as is. 3 refuted points, 4 minor ones.
REFUTED:
(1) Build script reruns on every build in a git worktree. crates/livtk-build/build.rs:73-77 watches packed-refs and refs/heads under --absolute-git-dir. In a worktree that is .git/worktrees/<name>, where neither exists, and cargo reruns on a missing file. cargo build -v, three times in a row: 'Dirty livtk-build: the file .git/worktrees/r16/packed-refs is missing'. That relinks livtk and livtk-app on every build. Separately, in a normal checkout, the script's own 'git status' rewrites .git/index (build.rs:31-45), so the next 1-3 builds rerun too. Fix: watch packed-refs and refs/ under --git-common-dir and HEAD/index under --git-dir, emit only paths that exist, and use 'git --no-optional-locks status'.
(2) BUILD is wrong in a shallow clone. 'git clone --depth 1' of a 7-commit repo gives 'build 1'. rev-list --count counts only the commits fetched (build.rs:26), so a CI-style clone would sort below every installed build, which breaks the ordering TAS-17 relies on. Nothing checks --is-shallow-repository.
(3) The acceptance asks for tests that the identity is set and ordered. There are none: crates/livtk-build has no tests, and cli.rs:539 and launch.rs:121 only compare --version against the binary's own constants, so 'build 0, unknown' would pass. The acceptance also says the old ~/.cargo/bin copies are named for removal. install_cli only names copies that come before ~/.local/bin on PATH (launch.rs:154, take_while), so on this Mac (.local/bin is before .cargo/bin) they are not named.
MINOR:
(a) 'modified' counts untracked files: 'git status --porcelain -- crates ...' lists ?? crates/.DS_Store, which exists in the real checkout, so every build on this Mac says modified even on a clean commit. Reproduced in a mini repo. Fix: add -uno or ignore .DS_Store.
(b) main.rs:13 uses std::env::args().nth(1), which panics on a non-UTF-8 first argument. The old code used args_os. Probe: panic at std env.rs:878, rc 101.
(c) install_cli: with a symlinked ~/.local/bin and its real folder on PATH, it says 'not on PATH' (launch.rs:153 compares paths literally). With PATH empty or unset, main.rs:120 falls back to '' and it reports a file called livtk in the current folder as shadowing. Linking into a bundle that lacks Contents/MacOS/livtk gives dangling links and exit 0 (main.rs:112 only checks that the bundle folder exists).
(d) Info.plist has no key for 'modified'.
UPHELD:
- Outside git: build 0, unknown, no reruns.
- A detached HEAD commit reruns the script (.git/HEAD), and so does a commit on a branch (index, refs/heads).
- A source change reruns it and sets modified. A .livtk/ change does neither.
- bundle-app with CARGO_TARGET_DIR: plutil -lint OK; CFBundleVersion 71, short version 0.4.0, LivtkCommit 1504213; codesign --verify --deep --strict passes (valid, satisfies its Designated Requirement); both binaries print '0.4.0 (build 71, 1504213, modified)'.
- The sed parsing is right for the plain, modified, unknown and -rc forms.
- install_cli: idempotent, replaces a link that points elsewhere, reports a shadow, handles a non-UTF-8 PATH.
- launch::start: probed current_exe on macOS. It is absolute even for a relative invocation and does not resolve links, so a link to a link gives Open, and a direct or relative run inside a bundle gives Bundled.
- The hooks claim holds on this Mac: hooks.json runs 'livtk', and Claude Code's PATH has ~/.local/bin before ~/.cargo/bin. It is not enforced, and is unverifiable for a Claude Code started from the GUI with launchd's PATH.
- scripts/check --install on macOS (read, not run): bundle-app --install, then the installed livtk-app --install-cli, which aborts the check under set -e if a file is in the way. Note that it rm -rf's a running ~/Applications/livtk.app.
scripts/check: every step passes except the CLI release benchmark (list median 11.7ms, budget 10ms) at load 18/30/37. That step passed 3 of 3 reruns at load 15-18. cargo-deny is not installed, so the supply chain was not checked.

After review 3 (refuted: (a) the palette's 'Add a note' named the selected row while the note went to the panel's node; (b) drafts were keyed by node id alone, so two open projects sharing ids, two clones of one repository, shared a draft; minor, older: c in the graph with no card focused the hidden note field): one rule in the model, Model::acted_on is the node open in the panel, else the selected row, so the note, the palette's labels and every action agree (s and x, which looked at the selection only and did nothing in the feed and the graph, follow it too); drafts are keyed by (project, node); c focuses the note field only when a panel opened. Tests: the palette's context names the panel's node (in a_note_goes_...), a_draft_stays_in_its_own_project (a clone with the same ids); each seen failing with its bug put back; every app test passes.

UNVERIFIABLE (live): whether bare key equivalents steal 'a' from 'g a'; menu flicker on setMainMenu while a menu is open; App Nap slowing the 200 ms poll while hidden (no prevent_app_nap); on_reopen fires only when no windows are open (platform.rs:1369), so with the window hidden it never fires and unhiding is AppKit's (the comment at mod.rs:250 is wrong); Windows set_dock_menu (jump list) not in the registry. scripts/check: format, lint and core/CLI pass; app tests fail only the_selection_glides_one_row_and_jumps_otherwise (ui.rs:2422, wall-clock), in 2/2 full runs and 1/3 alone; release bench list_of_10k 20-21 ms vs 10 ms; load 15-22; cargo-deny not installed. It watches .git/worktrees/<n>/{HEAD,index} and the common .git/{packed-refs,refs}, only paths that exist. (4) modified: untracked crates/.DS_Store files and a .livtk/ change leave it false; a tracked edit sets it, and reverting clears it. (A new .DS_Store still reruns the script, since crates/ is watched, but the output stays right.) data.text: Review fixes. (1) The Dock's items work with no window active: ui::dock_actions registers app-level handlers for New Task, Inbox and Project1..9 that bring the window forward and act in it; while the window is active its root handlers take the action first, so nothing runs twice. Test: after deactivate_window the Dock's Inbox is available and opens the inbox, New Task opens the form. (2) The poll makes the menus again (only when they changed), so the Dock's Inbox (n) is right while the window is hidden and draws nothing. (3) The shortcuts and About have the keys while shown (a focus handle on the modal), so a, 1-4, g sequences never act behind them; Esc closes them and the list has the keys again. Test. (4) New Task over the palette (or any overlay) closes it first; over an open form it keeps the half-typed text and focuses the title. Test. (5) The shortcuts modal lists Cmd+W only on macOS. (6) Not fixed: GPUI keeps every menu's actions it was ever given (macos platform.rs), ~1 KB per menu change, and the app sends menus only when what they show changes (view, layout, options, projects, inbox count), so it grows by human actions, not by time; an upstream fix. Comment on on_reopen corrected: it fires with no window shown; a window hidden by Cmd+W is shown again by AppKit. Live check wanted: whether the menus' bare key equivalents (A for Acknowledge, shown because those keys are bound in the list only) ever take a letter typed into a field or the second key of g a.

After review 4: a drag moves the panel to the card dragged, and a filter or a folded group that hides the selection moves selection and panel together to the first row shown (Model::reselect), so a, s, x and 1-4 act on the node in view. Changes from elsewhere still leave the panel where it is. Test: the_panel_follows_a_drag_a_filter_and_a_fold. The stray first line of track_note's comment removed.

After review 2: the build script also watches the git directory's shallow file, so git fetch --unshallow gives the right build number on the next build (its going away makes cargo run the script again), as the warning says.

Built. ui/state_flow.rs: StateFlow, a component of its own (kind, steps, arrows, what a choice does, the standing-rule menu), with a fixed height (PATH_HEIGHT), so the panel never jumps as the state changes. The current state: its mark larger (34 px against 22), filled in its state's colour and ringed in it, its glow coming in once when it becomes current, its label bold. The moves from here: dotted rings, in the accent where the move is the human's decision. Out of reach: faded. Arrows: the new arrow-right/left-stroke icons, lit along a move (accent for a decision), faint otherwise. States off the main path (parked, canceled) as pills on an Or row. The detail panel uses it; the old drawing is gone. Test: the current mark is the larger, every mark sits on one line, and after a move the flow keeps its height and the new state stands out instead. scripts/check passes.

Built. The detail panel's order is now title, state flow, properties, links (with + Add link), description, activity. Test: the_panels_links_come_before_the_description (the links' section ends above the description).

Built. The panel's Status is a button, as its Priority is: it opens the same state menu a row's or card's state icon opens (the kind's states, the moves from here enabled, the human's decisions in the accent, the rest greyed, the standing rule for a lesson), anchored in the panel. One state_button serves rows, cards and the panel (Menu::DetailState). The status now reads the state's full name (Acknowledged, In review) as the menus do. Kinds with no flow (findings) keep a plain status. Test: the_panels_status_opens_the_state_menu (opens, fits inside the panel, acknowledges the task, closes).

Plan (Claude), started on the developer's ack. Today the description already renders markdown (gpui-component's TextView), without code highlighting; notes are plain text. (1) Notes render markdown with the same view as the description. (2) Code blocks are highlighted by language (```rust …): gpui-component highlights them with tree-sitter when its grammars are compiled in, so livtk-app enables a chosen set of its tree-sitter features (rust, toml, json, yaml, bash, javascript, typescript/tsx, python, go, sql, diff, html, css, markdown); more can be added one feature at a time. A fence with another language or none shows as plain code. (3) The app's colours reach the markdown view: theme::apply edits the theme in place and never pushed it down (Theme::sync_base), so text views and scrollbars kept gpui-component's defaults. review 2: REFUTED (one regression, one latent hole); the rest UPHELD. Worktree at 1504213 + ALL-11.patch, probe UI tests (tests/zz_ui.rs, worktree only). Vision (Claude), for the developer to agree or correct before any plan. livtk is already event-sourced: every change is an event in events.jsonl. What is missing is a way for something outside (a sub-agent, a notifier, later a webhook) to hear the events that matter to it, reliably. (1) Signals: a small, stable, versioned vocabulary derived from raw events: node.created, node.moved (from, to), node.noted, node.edited, link.added/removed, and the meaningful ones: decision.needed (something entered a human gate), decision.made (acked/ratified/rejected/accepted), work.unblocked (what something waited for is done). Each signal carries the event id, node key, kind, actor, and a schema version that never breaks. (2) Pull first: livtk events --follow --json streams signals as newline-delimited JSON, with --since <cursor> and filters (--kind, --node, --signal, later --assignee). A consumer keeps its own cursor (the last event id), so delivery is at-least-once, in order, and idempotent by event id: a sub-agent that was asleep catches up exactly. (3) Push next: hooks declared per project in .livtk config (on: decision.made, run: <command>), getting the signal as JSON on stdin, run after the event is committed, never able to block or roll back a write; failures are logged and retried with a cursor. Webhooks are the same with a URL. (4) Assignment later: when nodes get an assignee, it is one more field on the signal and one more filter, so a sub-agent can wake on its own work only. Nothing in this batch changes how events are written. Question back: do you want push hooks in this batch, or pull (events --follow) first and hooks right after?

Vision (Claude), for the developer to agree or correct before any plan. Today one notice at a time sits bottom right, plain text, error or info, and long text runs past its edges. Proposal: one in-app notification system the whole app (and later settings) builds on. (1) A toast is: a level (info, success, warning, error), an optional title, a markdown body (wrapped, links and code rendered), an optional source (sync, install, inbox, update), and up to two actions (Open TAS-12, Retry, Copy details, Restart to Update). (2) Layout: fixed width, text wraps, never overflows; a long body is clipped to a few lines with Show more expanding it in place (scrolling past a max height). A coloured bar and icon by level, from theme tokens, readable in the app's palette. (3) Behaviour: they stack (newest on top, at most three, the rest counted as +N), keep today's rules (hover holds, closes with x, fades), and by level: info and success leave on their own, warnings stay longer, errors stay until closed. The same failure is not repeated, it is counted (x3). (4) Configurable later without changing callers: per-source and per-level settings (mute, duration, position), because every toast is raised through one API with its source and level. (5) Uses: errors and notices now; in the app, inbox arrivals while the window is in front (today those say nothing) and update available. Question back: should inbox arrivals while you are in the app become toasts in this batch, or stay silent for now?

data.text:
Developer's review (in chat): the flow looks cheap, the glow's box shadow most of all. Wanted instead, after a reference image (dark dotted grid, cards with thin corner arcs, a fine twisted light thread between them flaring at its ends): more delicate connections than arrows, and states that can be swiped. Agreed in chat: a swipe moves the task; labels in the app's own font, under the marks; parked and canceled on threads curving down; the same task, redone.

Plan (Claude), for the developer's ack:
(1) Look. The flow is a band on a faint dotted grid. States are their marks with their names under them in the app's font. The current state is framed by thin corner arcs in its colour (no shadow), a little larger than the rest. States out of reach are near ghosts (hairline outline, dim label).
(2) Threads, no arrows. Neighbouring states are joined by a fine curved thread drawn as two strands twisting past each other, painted with GPUI's path API. Not takeable from here: a faint hairline. Takeable: brighter, flaring to a small burst where it meets the state (layered strokes and ellipses, since GPUI cannot blur a path); in the accent where the move is the human's decision. Parked, canceled and rejected branch below on threads curving down from the path; the separate Or row goes.
(3) Motion, calm. Light drifts slowly along a takeable thread toward where it leads. When the state changes, the corner arcs glide to the new state and the thread it took lights once and settles. Nothing runs at rest: animation only while it plays, and none with the system's Reduce Motion setting on.
(4) Swipe. A two-finger swipe on the flow, or dragging the current state, pulls it along a thread toward a neighbour: the thread stretches and brightens, the target's name asks (Doing?). Let go past halfway: the task moves. Before that: it springs back. Toward a state it cannot reach: the thread stays faint, it resists and springs back with a small shake. Down: toward the branches. A click on a takeable state still moves it. After a move, a short Undo where the move back is legal; done and canceled ask once more before they are made.
(5) Still one component (ui/state_flow.rs) with a fixed height, fitting the narrowest panel; the standing-rule menu for lessons kept.
Tests: the current state is framed and the largest; height fixed in every state of every kind; the narrowest panel fits; a drag past halfway toward a takeable state moves the task, short of it or toward an untakeable one does not; a swipe does the same; clicks still move; the branches sit below the path; Reduce Motion means no animation. Acceptance: scripts/check passes, and the developer finds it alive, not cheap, in the app.
The developer agreed to the plan above in chat ("Sure, well aligned let's go"), its undo, confirmation, resistance, Reduce Motion and the Or row's going included.

data.text: Built, as planned. ui/state_flow/ is the component and its geometry (geometry.rs: plain arithmetic, tested in tests/flow.rs). Look: a faint dotted field; states as small circles with their names under them in the app's font; the current state larger, faintly filled and framed by two thin corner arcs in its colour (no shadow); reachable states ringed (the accent for the human's decision), the rest ghosts. Threads: two strands of a cubic twisting past each other between neighbours, a hairline when idle; lit, a layered glow (GPUI blurs no path) and a flare where they arrive. Parked and canceled hang on a line below, a thread curving down to each from the current state, leaving below the labels; from a state below, threads rise only to the states it can go back to. The Or row is gone. Motion: the arcs glide to a new state (380 ms); light drifts along lit threads only while the pointer is over the flow or pulls it (40 fps cap); with Reduce Motion nothing animates: the app asks the system (macOS defaults, GNOME gsettings) at start and whenever its window comes forward, off the main thread, and sets GPUI's reduce_motion, which its animations honour; tests set it themselves. Pull: drag the current state, or swipe sideways on the trackpad (an upright swipe stays the panel's scrolling). A pull keeps to a lane: sideways along the line the state is on, up or down across to the other. Past halfway along a reachable thread it moves; short, it springs back (280 ms); toward a state out of reach it gives at most 10 px and shakes back. A click on a reachable state still moves. Done and canceled ask (Keep / Move). After a move from the flow, a notice says where the task is now with Undo, when the move back is allowed (Model::move_in_flow, Notice.undo). Tests: geometry (order, lines, fit at 320 px, threads and their light, lanes, halfway, resistance, a pull down), UI (pull short and past halfway, Undo, upright and sideways swipes, done asks, drift only under the pointer and never with Reduce Motion, branches below, the frame following a pull after a move). scripts/check passes. Live: does it feel alive and not cheap; the swipe's direction on your trackpad.
