data.text: review: REFUTED (one defect against the plan's 'nothing runs at rest', and one smaller one). Tests flow/ui/model pass (8/36/94). (1) A swipe whose Ended never comes leaves a pull stuck, so the light keeps drifting at 40 fps with the pointer away, on every node, until the next mouse pull. When two fingers rest on the trackpad and lift without moving, macOS sends MayBegin then Cancelled. gpui-pre-macos events.rs:259-265 maps MayBegin to TouchPhase::Started and Cancelled to Moved (only Ended maps to Ended). state_flow/mod.rs:339-343 sets drag = Swipe{sideways:false} on Started, a zero Moved never clears it, and drifting = hovered || drag.is_some() (mod.rs:271). Reproduced: Started(0,0), Moved(0,0), pointer moved to (3,3) -> flow-drift drawn, and it is still drawn after j. Control: with no wheel events, or with an Ended, there is no drift. The TouchPhase::Cancelled arm (mod.rs:383) is never reached on macOS. A stuck pull is also not reset by the next swipe's Started (mod.rs:340, if st.drag.is_none()), and Started's begin() withdraws an open Done?/Canceled? question even on an upright scroll over the flow (mod.rs:114). (2) A pull outlives a change of node: FlowState::see (mod.rs:103-106) clears glide and confirm for another node but not drag. Reproduced: mouse down on LIV-1's flow-planned, press j, move 0.8 of the gap right, release -> LIV-2 becomes Acked and LIV-1 stays Planned. Upheld: pulling or swiping a lesson to Ratified opens the standing menu and moves nothing (menu Some(standing), state Proposed), and ratify-standing then gives Ratified with 1 rule. A move with no Undo clears the previous notice (planned->acked Undo notice, then ->parked: notice None), so no stale Undo. Undo is taken from the notice (model.rs:1052). Geometry: a zero distance between overlapping nodes gives NaN cos, which the filter (geometry.rs:312) drops, and one main state centres, so no panic. Reduce Motion tests set it themselves and open_app never calls follow_system, so they do not depend on the machine. At rest with no pointer there is no flow-drift. Smells: a stale doc stacked on move_in_flow (model/flow.rs:172-173 is choose_on's old doc), and FlowState::pulling 'for tests' (mod.rs:89) is used nowhere. Live only: whether it feels alive and not cheap; the swipe direction; a Canceled? confirmation at the branch line (top ~114 of a 132 band) hanging past the band over the body.

After review: (1) a trackpad touch is only a pull once it moves sideways past 4 px; until then it is held apart (FlowState.touch), so fingers resting and lifting without a move (macOS sends them no Ended: GPUI maps MayBegin to Started and Cancelled to Moved) leave no pull, no drift and no withdrawn question; each new touch ends a swipe's pull that never ended, a mouse's is left alone; Cancelled lets go without moving. (2) Showing another node drops a pull, a touch and a spring-back begun on the last one, so a pull never lands on another task. (3) The question for canceled (on the line below) sits over its state, inside the flow. Smells: move_in_flow's stale comment and the unused FlowState::pulling are gone. Tests: a_touch_that_never_ends_leaves_nothing_behind, a_pull_does_not_carry_over_to_another_task. scripts/check passes.

Developer's review (in chat): impressed overall; but (1) the stick at each thread's end looks cheap: remove it; (2) instead of the thin framing of the current state, a slight box shadow of its colour; (3) swiping has no transitions and feels cheap; (4) remove swiping entirely and keep clicking; (5) a state becoming current should transition, growing nicely.

Done as reviewed: the flare at the threads' ends is gone; the current state is faintly filled in its colour with a soft glow of it (a box shadow, 10 px blur), the corner arcs gone; dragging and swiping are gone (with their geometry: Pull, lanes, resistance, the touch handling), a click is the way to move. On a move the new state grows into the current one (420 ms, easing out just past its size and settling) as its glow comes up, while the state it left settles back to the others' size; with Reduce Motion both are at their end at once. Done and canceled still ask; Undo still follows a move. Tests: a_clicked_state_becomes_the_larger_and_a_drag_moves_nothing (sizes at the end, a drag moves nothing, Undo); end-state tests pin Reduce Motion so the clock never decides them. scripts/check passes.

Developer, in chat: straight threads along the path except those touching the current state, which keep their twist; the threads a little alive, a barely noticeable movement; no dotted grid. Done: Thread.twist (touches the current state, or goes to or from the line below); the rest of the path is one straight hairline (or a straight lit line). The twisting strands breathe, out of step with each other and thread to thread (about 22% of their 3 px twist, twice in 12 s), drawn at most 24 frames a second at rest (40 while light drifts under the pointer); off with Reduce Motion. The dotted field is gone. Cost to know: while a panel is open and motion is on, the window redraws at that rate. Test: threads_touching_the_current_state_twist_and_the_rest_of_the_path_is_straight. scripts/check passes.

Tests flow/ui/model pass (6/36/92), clippy -D warnings clean on livtk-app. Drag/swipe gone from state_flow/ (no TouchPhase, ScrollWheel, Pull, lanes, touch; README/docs never mention swiping; the 'Drag' shortcut row at ui/mod.rs:222 is the board's, not the flow's); a drag on a state moves nothing (test). Built. One change from the plan, in where code lives: the updater is its own crate, livtk-update (a library and the helper binary), not livtk-core::update, so the task store stays the task store. Contract: Manifest format 1 (unknown fields ignored, a newer format skipped, sha256 and a plain artifact path checked), ordered by build number; Source trait with LocalFolder (newest build for this app, platform and arch; a bad manifest never hides the rest). Staging: size, SHA-256, ditto unpack, and the bundle's identifier and build checked against the manifest. The helper, livtk-update, fixed command line (--pid --installed --staged --health --build [--wait]): waits for the app to exit, moves the staged app beside the installed one, swaps by renames in one folder, starts it with LIVTK_UPDATE_HEALTH set, and keeps it once it writes its build number there, else moves it out, puts the old one back and starts it. The app: looks at launch, every 6 hours and from Check for Updates…; stages off the main thread; offers Restart to Update in the livtk menu and the sidebar (never on its own); on it starts the helper and quits; started after an update it reports healthy and says once what changed. scripts/bundle-app puts livtk-update in the bundle; scripts/release [--quick] [notes] zips the bundle and writes the manifest into the local source. Tests: manifests, the source's choice, verification, staging a real zipped bundle, swap and rollback, the menu offering Restart only when staged. scripts/check passes.

review: REFUTED (one data-loss path, two wrong-behaviour paths). (1) crates/livtk-update/src/swap.rs:53 launch(&s.installed)? after the swap returns Err with no rollback: the unverified new build stays installed, the old app sits hidden at .livtk.app-previous, nothing is running; the next update's remove(&previous) at swap.rs:43 deletes it, so the original app is lost for good. Repro (probe test, temp dir): launch -> Err("open failed") gives Err, installed=new, dir=[.livtk.app-previous, livtk.app]; a second swap leaves only livtk.app=new plus .livtk.app-failed. Same at swap.rs:52 (remove_file(health) failing). Fix: on any error after line 48, roll back as for an unhealthy start. Rollback's own launch failing (swap.rs:63) leaves the old app in place, which is fine. (2) Rollback never stops the new build (swap.rs:58-63). A build that is slow or hung rather than crashed keeps running from .livtk.app-failed, and open -a on the old bundle with the same identifier may only bring the running one forward (launch.rs:83-84 says so itself), so the old build never starts. Needs a live run; the fix is to kill the new process (or wait for it to exit) before restoring. (3) The rolled-back old build is started with LIVTK_UPDATE_HEALTH too (main.rs:55-63), so report_started (updates.rs:56-61, ui/mod.rs:298) writes the old build and the app says 'Updated to <old build>' after a rollback. Also launch::passed_on (launch.rs:70) forwards every LIVTK_* var, so LIVTK_UPDATE_HEALTH leaks on to anything the updated app opens. report_started should only claim an update when this build is the one the helper asked for (pass --build in a second var, or compare). Minor: manifest.rs:93 rejects '..' but takes an absolute artifact path (probe: artifact /etc/hosts parses, LocalFolder resolves it to /etc/hosts; the hash still guards it, but it breaks the 'beside the manifest' contract). ui/mod.rs:1494-1497's doc says a development build looks only when asked, but run() checks unconditionally (mod.rs:305), so a dev build shares and can rm -rf the installed app's staging dir. An asked check while staged (mod.rs:1516) re-stages build-N with remove_dir_all under the Staged path the menu holds, so Restart during that window swaps in a partial bundle. Fine: the swap when installed is missing (Err, nothing touched except staged moved to .incoming); the copy fallback when rename fails (forced with a 0555 staging dir: Updated, relative links fine, absolute links copied verbatim and pointing into staging); a stale health file (removed before launch, swap.rs:52); the pid wait (gives up after 30s, nothing changed); argument parsing (missing or invalid gives usage and exit 2); restart_to_update outside a bundle (warns, no quit); the 6-hour loop does not re-stage once staged; scripts/release quoting (plutil per field, notes safe) and a dirty tree (warns, keeps HEAD's number). Tests: livtk-update 6/6, livtk-app --test app 173 passed. Live only: (2), Gatekeeper and first-launch time against the 20s wait, open --env reaching the app, quit finishing within 30s.

After review: every failure after the swap rolls back (a new build that cannot be started included), so the old app is never lost; a build that does not start well is stopped first (its program signalled) and the old one started as a new instance (open -n), not asked to report, so it never claims to be an update; an interrupted earlier swap gets its old app back first; LIVTK_UPDATE_HEALTH is never passed on; an absolute artifact path is refused; only the installed app looks for updates (a development build never touches its staging); Check for Updates… on a staged build says so instead of unpacking it again. The swap takes a Launcher (start, stop), so each path is tested: launch failure, rollback twice in a row, an interrupted swap. Left for a live run: whether a first launch fits the 20 s wait under Gatekeeper.

Plan (Claude), for the developer's ack.
Goal: a sub-list written in a body or a note shows as a nested list.
Findings so far: gpui's markdown parser (markdown-rs, CommonMark) keeps nested lists as nested nodes, so the fault is either in how gpui draws a nested list item, or in what livtk feeds it: a sub-list in CommonMark needs its marker indented under the parent's text (two spaces under '- '), and Tab does not indent in livtk's fields today (TAS-32); notes also pass through note_markdown, which adds hard breaks.
Approach: reproduce in the running app with '- a' / '  - b' / '    - c' in a body and in a note; find the layer at fault; fix it there (note_markdown never touching list lines; or a small livtk-side render of nested items if gpui draws them flat, with an upstream issue noted). Behaviour test: note_markdown leaves list structure alone.
Acceptance: two and three levels of bullets and numbered lists nest visibly in bodies and notes; scripts/check passes.

Plan (Claude), for the developer's ack.
Goal: Tab indents and Shift+Tab outdents in the task body editor and the note field, as in a code editor; with several lines selected, all of them.
Findings: the text area already binds Tab to indent and Shift+Tab to outdent in its own key context; in livtk something takes Tab first (GPUI's focus navigation, or a binding of livtk's), so Tab leaves the field instead.
Approach: find what takes Tab and let the text areas keep it; indent by two spaces, which is also what a markdown sub-list needs (TAS-33); the title field and the filter keep Tab as it is. Behaviour test: Tab in the body editor and the note field inserts the indent and the focus stays.
Acceptance: Tab/Shift+Tab indent and outdent in bodies and notes; scripts/check passes.

Plan (Claude), for the developer's ack.
Goal: sub-tasks show under their parent in the list, indented, without breaking filtering, grouping or ordering.
Experience:
- List: a sub-task sits right below its parent, indented one step, with the turn icon (bx-turn-down, turned as a ↳) leading it. A parent shows its sub-tasks' progress (2/3) and a small caret that folds them; folded parents remember it per view.
- Grouping: a sub-task nests only when it falls in the same group as its parent (same state, or same priority). Otherwise it stays in its own group, at its place, with a quiet ↳ TAS-12 chip naming its parent, so a group never shows work of another state.
- Ordering: the parent's place is decided by the view's ordering; its sub-tasks follow it, ordered the same way among themselves.
- Filtering: a sub-task that matches while its parent does not shows on its own, with its parent chip; a parent that matches shows only the sub-tasks that match too.
- Board: cards stay in their columns (no nesting there); a sub-task card carries the parent chip, a parent card its progress.
- Keys: j/k walk the rows as drawn; Enter on a parent opens it as today; the caret folds with a click. A View option, 'Nest sub-tasks', on by default, turns nesting off.
Model: arrange() orders rows into parent-then-children blocks within each group; one level for now (a sub-sub-task nests under its parent the same way, indented once more, up to three).
Tests: model behaviour (nesting only within a group, filter cases, ordering, folding); no visual tests.
Acceptance: the cases above hold in the app; scripts/check passes.

Plan (Claude), from the vision the developer agreed (pull first, then push), for the developer's ack.
Part 1, pull (built first):
- livtk-core::signal: a small, versioned vocabulary derived from the event log, never stored: node.created, node.moved {from, to}, node.noted, node.edited, link.added, link.removed, and the meaningful ones: decision.needed (a node entered a human gate), decision.made (acknowledged, ratified, accepted, rejected, retired), work.unblocked (the last thing a node waited for is done). Each signal: {v: 1, signal, event (its event id: the cursor), at, by, node, key, kind, and the signal's own fields}. v only ever grows; readers ignore fields they do not know.
- CLI: livtk events [--since <event id>] [--follow] [--signal S]... [--kind K] [--node KEY]: newline-delimited JSON, in log order. --follow keeps watching (the app's cheap refresh, every 200 ms). A consumer keeps its own cursor, so delivery is at least once, in order, and idempotent by event id: a sub-agent that slept catches up exactly.
Part 2, push (after part 1 is in use):
- In .livtk/config.toml, [[on]] signal = "decision.made", run = ["cmd", ...]: run after the event is committed, with the signal's JSON on stdin, never able to block or undo a write; a failure is logged and retried from a cursor kept per hook. Webhooks later are the same with a URL.
Later: an assignee is one more field and one more filter, so a sub-agent wakes on its own work.
Tests: each signal from its events (work.unblocked with several dependencies), cursors (since, resume, idempotence), the CLI's filters and --follow picking up a write from another process; for push, a hook run once per signal, a failing hook retried and never blocking the write.
Acceptance: Claude can run livtk events --follow --signal decision.made in one session and see the human's acknowledgement from the app arrive; scripts/check passes.

Plan (Claude), from the vision the developer agreed (inbox arrivals in the app become notifications), for the developer's ack.
- One notification model for the app (replacing Notice): level (info, success, warning, error), optional title, a markdown body, a source (sync, update, install, inbox, the app), up to two actions (Open TAS-12, Retry, Restart to Update, Copy details), a count for repeats. Raised through one API (model.notify(Note::error(...).title(...).action(...))); warn and inform become thin calls into it, so nothing calling them changes.
- Behaviour: they stack, newest on top, three shown and the rest counted (+N); the same notification again counts up (×3) instead of stacking; how long each stays by level (info and success 6 s, warning 10 s, error until closed); the pointer holds one, as today; × closes it.
- View: a fixed width, the text wrapping, never past an edge; a long body clipped to four lines with Show more, which opens it in place and scrolls past a height; a bar and an icon in the level's colour from the theme; the actions as small buttons.
- Inbox arrivals while the window is in front become an info notification (TAS-12 waits for you · Open); while it is away, the system notification as today.
- Configurable later without touching callers: a policy (per source and level: muted, how long) the settings will fill; today's defaults are that policy.
Tests: behaviour in the model (stacking and +N, repeats counting, lifetimes by level, holding, an action running, inbox arrivals in front vs away); no visual tests.
Acceptance: errors, notices, updates and inbox arrivals all show through it, long text never overflows; scripts/check passes.

Built (on the developer's yes in chat, ahead of the ack). Cause: livtk's body editor, note field and the new task's body grow with their text, and gpui's text area indents only fields of a fixed height: in a growing one it passes Tab on, and gpui's Root moves the focus. Now those three fields take Tab and Shift+Tab themselves (one undoable edit over every line the selection touches): a list item indents to the text of the item above, making it a sub-item, and outdents back one level; any other line by two spaces. Tests: the reindent rules (model), Tab in a real note field indenting and keeping the focus.

Built with TAS-32 (on the developer's yes in chat, ahead of the ack). Cause: gpui parses and draws nested lists (a nested list inside an item, indented); what failed was the input: a sub-item must start under its parent's text (2 spaces under '- ', 3 under '1. ', 4 under '10. ') and Tab could not indent. Tab now indents a list item to exactly that column, so sub-lists nest in bodies and notes, numbered ones included. Tests: indents for -, 1., 10. markers, one level deeper and back.

review: REFUTED. (1) A repeat strands a held notification forever. toasts.rs:136-142 keeps held=true but gives the toast a new id and moves it to the top; the view names cards by id (ui/mod.rs:5007-5012, 'toast-{id}' or 'notice'), so the hovered element disappears and no on_hover(false) ever reaches it (ui/mod.rs:5122-5125). age() skips held ones (toasts.rs:200, 211), so it never leaves. Repro (headless UI probe): notify info A, notify info B, move the pointer onto toast-{A}, notify A again (it jumps to the top, away from the pointer), move the pointer to 10,10, age 60 s: B is gone, A is still shown. Model-only version: hold(a,true); raise(A) gives a2!=a; hold(a,false) does nothing; age +200 s, A remains. (2) A repeat collapses an expanded one: expanded is keyed by id (ui/mod.rs:5032, 5070), the id changes on a repeat, and the old id stays in the set (it grows by one per expansion, never pruned; trivial). (3) told() (ui/mod.rs:6289) looks only at the shown three, so a hidden one leaving changes +N with no repaint. Repro: info, then 3 errors; age +7 s/+8 s: age() returns true, told() identical, more 1->0, and the poll (ui/mod.rs:704-711) does not cx.notify, so '+1 more' stays drawn. Also: hidden info/success notifications age out unseen behind three errors. (4) Errors now never leave, but a sync or catch-up failure that recovers is not closed: went() (model.rs:243) only tells failures, and clear_errors runs only after a human's command succeeds (model.rs:892/924). So 'proj: <failure>' stays after sync works again; failures whose text changes each time stack without limit (probe: 50 distinct errors, all still there an hour later). A lasting identical failure is told once (went dedups), so there is no per-tick pile. OK: same level/title/text counted; held is kept across a repeat in the model; tell_quiet behaves as before (it only runs at startup); Act::Open selects arrival.project by index, the same as notifications posted while away. cargo test -p livtk-app --test app: 179 pass. After review: a repeat keeps its id (count up, time again, to the top), so what the pointer holds and Show more stay with it; only the shown three age, one below them waits its turn rather than leaving unseen; at most 20 are kept; the view repaints when a count or the +N changes, and Show more forgets notifications that are gone; a project's failure is raised with its source and taken back once the project works again (tick and catch-up). Part 1, pull, built. livtk-core::signal: Signals derives the vocabulary (v 1) from the log through a small projection (each node's key, kind and state, what it waits for), so a reader's signals are right from any cursor: node.created, node.moved {from, to}, node.edited {fields}, node.noted {text}, link.added/removed {rel, other}, decision.needed {state} (into planned, proposed, or a gate's from-state), decision.made {from, to} (a human-only move, gates included), work.unblocked (the last open thing a node waited for closed, or the dependency was removed). Store/Workspace::events_after(cursor). CLI: livtk events [--since EVENT] [--follow] [--signal S]... [--kind K] [--node KEY], JSON lines; --follow re-reads every 200 ms. Tests: core (a plan's decision needed then made, unblocked only when the last dependency closes, reading on from a cursor) and the CLI (--since, and --follow seeing a write from another process). README: Signals. Next: part 2, push (hooks).

Part 2, push, built. livtk-core::on: [[on]] entries (signal, run, optional kind) in .livtk/config.toml. Workspace::dispatch runs each hook for the signals it has not heard, its JSON on stdin, from the project's folder, 30 s at most per run; a hook's cursor (.livtk/on-state.json, local, git-ignored, written whole) moves past an event only once every signal of it succeeded, so a failing hook is retried in order and misses nothing; a hook seen for the first time hears from the write that woke it on (the CLI passes the newest event before its write), never the history; one dispatcher at a time (.livtk/on.lock, try-lock: a second leaves the work to the first). Callers: the CLI, after any command that wrote, starts 'livtk dispatch' detached and returns at once; the app dispatches off its window after its own writes. Tests: a new hook hears only what comes, a failing hook retried missing nothing in order, a second dispatcher leaving the work, the .gitignore kept, and from the CLI a write running a hook added after the first write. Found by a test on the way: a hook added to an empty project was taken as new twice and skipped what came between; fixed. README: hooks.

review: REFUTED (6b2a6d2; targeted tests pass: signal+on 13/1 ignored, cli 3+3). Reproduced with debug livtk in /tmp projects:
(1) Lost wakeup: a write made while a dispatcher holds on.lock is never dispatched until some later write. on.rs:85 a second dispatcher returns busy, and the running one computed its events once at on.rs:90 and never looks again. Repro: a node.noted hook doing 'sleep 3'; 'livtk note T-1 x'; 0.5 s later 'livtk new c' with a node.created hook; 5 s later, with no dispatcher running, the hook still had not heard T-3. It only arrived on the next unrelated write. The claim 'misses nothing' fails for any concurrent writer, and for the app plus an agent.
(2) Pulled or merged events are skipped for good. Cursors compare UUIDv7 order (on.rs:106 '*e > cursor', store.rs:519 'id > ?1 ORDER BY id', main.rs:575 events --follow), so an event from another clone with an older timestamp, merged in after the cursor moved on, falls behind every cursor. Repro: cp the project to p2; 'new fromB' in p2; then 'new fromA' in p1 with a node.created hook and 'events --follow' running; append p2's line to p1's events.jsonl (a git pull); 'new after-merge'. Neither the hook nor the follower ever saw fromB's node.created. 'A sub-agent that slept catches up exactly' does not hold across a git pull.
(3) After that merge, signal keys are wrong. signal.rs:117/121 take the key from the create event, not the key the node resolved to. Both fromA and fromB come out as key T-4 in 'livtk events' (fromA is T-5 in 'list'), and every later signal about fromA says T-4, so a consumer acting by key touches the wrong node.
(4) A spurious work.unblocked: signal.rs:234-238 emit it when any depends_on edge is removed, even when the node had no open dependencies left. Repro (human): 'dep add T-1 --on T-2'; 'move T-2 canceled' (unblocked, correct); 'dep rm T-1 --on T-2' gives a second work.unblocked for T-1. It should fire only when the removed dependency was still open.
(5) A hook that writes through livtk is not loop-free, only throttled by bug (1). A node.noted hook running 'livtk note T-1 echo' gave 2 notes after the first write and 5 after the second, so each outside write runs one more echo than the last, without bound. Nothing stops a hook from hearing its own writes.
Minor: the app calls ws.dispatch(), not dispatch_from(before) (livtk-app ui/mod.rs:5181), so a hook first seen from the app skips the write that woke it, unlike the CLI. take_written's Vec::dedup (model.rs:1113) drops only adjacent repeats. A corrupt on-state.json is silently reset to 'from now on' (on.rs:158), dropping pending retries without a word. A changed [[on]] entry leaves its old cursor in on-state.json forever. Gate 'kind: -> to' (from any state) never yields decision.needed (signal.rs:92 needs g.from == Some(state)), only decision.made.
Held up: no [[on]] means dispatch creates no files; read-only commands (list, show, events) spawn no dispatcher; edit of an acked task gives node.edited, node.moved acked->planned and decision.needed; a corrupt state file does not crash; the hung-hook kill is bounded at 30 s; a hook that reads no stdin is fine; on.rs is portable (std File::try_lock; cfg(unix) only on tests).

data.text: After review: (1) the dispatcher reads on until nothing new is left and looks once more after letting go of its lock, so a write made while hooks ran is heard in that run (test: a write landing mid-run). (2) A hook's state is what it heard: everything older than a horizon, and the events it handled within 30 days, so an older event merged in from elsewhere is still heard (test: a clone's acknowledgement merged in after a newer one here); livtk events --follow likewise prints every event it has not printed, rereading the log when it changes. (3) Signals carry the node's key as it stands when read (a merge renumbers); consumers act on node, which never changes. (4) work.unblocked on a dependency's removal only when the node was blocked (test). (5) A hook runs with LIVTK_HOOK: livtk inside it acts as claude:hook (never the human, so it passes none of the human's gates) and starts no dispatcher, and no hook hears what a hook did (test). Also: the app passes the newest event before its write, as the CLI does; an unreadable state is reported and each hook hears from then on; state for entries no longer in the config is dropped. A gate from any state makes nothing wait (as the inbox), so it signals decision.made but not decision.needed.
