data.title: livtk can drive Claude runs headless: stream-json by session id, permissions routed to notes, runs outlive the app
data.body:
Tried on this machine, Claude Code 2.1.280, 2026-10-21, with haiku and tiny prompts in a scratch git repo.

What holds:
- `claude -p PROMPT --session-id UUID --output-format stream-json --verbose < /dev/null` streams one JSON object a line: system hook_started/hook_response, system init (session_id, tools, agents, permissionMode), assistant (thinking, text, tool_use), user (tool_result), rate_limit_event, then one `result` (subtype success | error_during_execution, result text, session_id, num_turns, permission_denials, terminal_reason). Without `< /dev/null` it waits 3 s for stdin and prints a non-JSON warning.
- `--resume UUID` continues the same session (same session_id), with a new prompt as the next message.
- `--permission-prompts none`: anything that would ask is refused automatically, the turn goes on, and `result.permission_denials` lists each refused tool with its exact input (tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_input). Resuming with `--allowedTools "Bash(<exact command>)"` lets exactly that run. A compound command (`a && b`) is checked part by part: allow each simple command, not the whole line.
- `--agent livtk:implementer` (a plugin agent) runs as the session's own agent; hooks receive `agent_type: livtk:implementer`, the session_id and permission_mode.
- An environment variable set for the run (LIVTK_TASK=KEY) reaches its hooks; UserPromptSubmit fires as a turn starts and Stop as it ends, without the session doing anything.
- A run started in its own process group (`start_new_session`) with its stream going to a file keeps working after the process that started it exits, and finishes on its own (a pipe to a dead parent would kill it).
- SIGINT to the run's process group ends it in under a second, exit 0, the stream closing with a `result` of subtype `error_during_execution`; the session then resumes by id.
- `claude --bg PROMPT` prints a short id (`backgrounded · 2fc4d938`); `claude agents --json --cwd DIR [--all]` lists it (id, kind background, state working|stopped, status busy, sessionId, name, cwd, waitingFor); `claude stop ID` stops it. It cannot take `-p`/stream-json, so livtk cannot read its turns or route its permissions.

Not tried: AskUserQuestion headless (a question in the final text reads as the run waiting for the human instead).

data.text: Amended by the spike (TAS-66, FND-1; docs/research/agents.md "What the spike settled"): the runner is livtk's own headless `claude -p --session-id --output-format stream-json --permission-prompts none`, started in its own process group with its stream to a file under .livtk/runs/ (local), not the --bg supervisor. Needs you = the result's permission_denials, written as a note with Allow/Deny; Allow resumes with --allowedTools for each simple command; a reply note resumes with --resume and the note; stop = SIGINT to the group (clean result, resumable); runs survive a quit on their own and are picked up by session id. The rest of the plan stands.

Done: all of the plan's questions answered on this machine (FND-1 has the commands and output shapes). The runner choice is named in docs/research/agents.md ("What the spike settled") and TAS-67 is amended by note. Scratch runs were in a temp git repo, now removed; one background session started for the test was stopped.

review: Check 1 (FND-1 records what holds and what does not, with versions and commands, for every plan question): REFUTED in part. Version (Claude Code 2.1.280, matches `claude --version`) and most commands are there. Covered: stream-json output shape and --resume by session id; --agent livtk:implementer as the session agent; --bg (prints id, `claude agents --json --cwd [--all]` fields, `claude stop ID`); LIVTK_TASK reaching hooks; a detached run (own process group, stream to file) outliving its parent; SIGINT stop with a clean result that can be resumed. Missing: (a) `--input-format stream-json` is in the plan but FND-1 never says whether it holds; every recorded command is `-p PROMPT < /dev/null`. (b) "Permission mode per stage" is not recorded; it only says hooks receive permission_mode, and nothing about --permission-mode for plan/build/review. (c) The plan asked which of --permission-prompt-tool (MCP) or PreToolUse defer answers cleanly. FND-1 uses a third route (--permission-prompts none, then permission_denials, then resume with --allowedTools) and does not say whether either named option was tried. AskUserQuestion is marked not tried. (d) "Picked up again by session id when the app comes back" is only shown for a run that was stopped and then resumed. Re-attaching to a run that is still going (finding its process or stream file by session id) is not shown, and the outlive test is described as Python `start_new_session` rather than a command. Check 2 (doc and amendments): UPHELD. docs/research/agents.md "What the spike settled" (629b411) names the runner (livtk-owned headless claude -p, not --bg). TAS-67 is amended by note. One caveat: the doc presents "a turn that ends on a question waits for your note" as settled, but FND-1 says AskUserQuestion was not tried.

data.body:
Tried on this machine, Claude Code 2.1.280, 2026-10-21, with haiku and tiny prompts in a scratch git repo.

What holds:
- `claude -p PROMPT --session-id UUID --output-format stream-json --verbose < /dev/null` streams one JSON object a line: system hook_started/hook_response, system init (session_id, tools, agents, permissionMode), assistant (thinking, text, tool_use), user (tool_result), rate_limit_event, then one `result` (subtype success | error_during_execution, result text, session_id, num_turns, permission_denials, terminal_reason). Without `< /dev/null` it waits 3 s for stdin and prints a non-JSON warning.
- `--resume UUID` continues the same session (same session_id), with a new prompt as the next message.
- `--permission-prompts none`: anything that would ask is refused automatically, the turn goes on, and `result.permission_denials` lists each refused tool with its exact input (tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_input). Resuming with `--allowedTools "Bash(<exact command>)"` lets exactly that run. A compound command (`a && b`) is checked part by part: allow each simple command, not the whole line.
- `--agent livtk:implementer` (a plugin agent) runs as the session's own agent; hooks receive `agent_type: livtk:implementer`, the session_id and permission_mode.
- An environment variable set for the run (LIVTK_TASK=KEY) reaches its hooks; UserPromptSubmit fires as a turn starts and Stop as it ends, without the session doing anything.
- A run started in its own process group (`start_new_session`) with its stream going to a file keeps working after the process that started it exits, and finishes on its own (a pipe to a dead parent would kill it).
- SIGINT to the run's process group ends it in under a second, exit 0, the stream closing with a `result` of subtype `error_during_execution`; the session then resumes by id.
- `claude --bg PROMPT` prints a short id (`backgrounded · 2fc4d938`); `claude agents --json --cwd DIR [--all]` lists it (id, kind background, state working|stopped, status busy, sessionId, name, cwd, waitingFor); `claude stop ID` stops it. It cannot take `-p`/stream-json, so livtk cannot read its turns or route its permissions.

Also tried, after review (same day, same version):
- `--input-format stream-json`: two user messages written to stdin as `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."}}` lines are answered in turn by one process, in one session, each with its own `result`. So a run can stay open and take your notes as they come, or be resumed per note; both hold.
- Permission mode per stage: `--permission-mode plan` does not suit a headless run. ExitPlanMode is not available headless, so the session cannot leave plan mode; it ran out of turns and wrote its plan to ~/.claude/plans/ rather than the project. Planning runs should use the default mode with `--permission-prompts none` and read-only tools allowed (Read, Grep, Glob, and `Bash(livtk *)` for its notes). Builds: the default mode, or acceptEdits inside a worktree. Reviews: read-only tools, as planning.
- The routes for a permission: PreToolUse `defer` holds (a hook answering `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"defer"}}` ends the turn with stop_reason `tool_deferred`), but its result is empty and lists nothing; what was deferred must come from the hook's own input. `--permission-prompts none` lists every refused tool with its exact input in the result, so livtk uses that. `--permission-prompt-tool` needs an MCP server for livtk to answer from; not tried, since the route above needs none.
- AskUserQuestion is not offered to a headless session at all; asked to use it, the session says so in its reply text. A question to the human comes as the turn's final text, so a turn that ends on a question is the run waiting for a note.
- Picking up a run that is still going: started in its own process group with its stream to a file (in Rust, `Command::process_group(0)` with stdout to the file; in a test, Python's `start_new_session=True`), it is found again by its session id (`pgrep -f "session-id <id>"` gives the pid, whose process group is its own), its file read from where the app left off, and read on to its `result` as it comes.

data.text: Review gaps closed (FND-1 amended, "Also tried, after review"): --input-format stream-json holds (two messages, one process, one session); plan mode does not suit headless runs (ExitPlanMode unavailable, plan written to ~/.claude/plans; the stray test file there was removed), so stages use default mode with read-only tools for planning and review; PreToolUse defer holds but lists nothing, --permission-prompt-tool not tried (needs an MCP server), so --permission-prompts none stays the route; AskUserQuestion is absent headless, questions come as final text; a run still going is found by session id (pgrep, own process group) and its stream file read on to its result. The doc says the same.

data.title: Clean up the app's seams: one table per view, one icon map, shared form parts, one duration format
data.body:
## Why
The human asked whether the icon change (TAS-72) was done to scale. An audit (2026-10-21) found smells, most added recently:
- the kind/view to icon mapping lives twice (`view_icon`, `kind_slot` in ui/mod.rs);
- a new view touches six places (View enum, GoX action, key binding, menu item with a hard-coded index `view(3)`, palette entry, icon);
- the Agents page copied settings.rs's form parts (`segmented`, `choice`, `button`, `field`);
- the duration format exists in the CLI (project.rs `span`) and the app (ui/mod.rs `span`);
- declared kinds all get one generic icon, with no way to choose;
- ui/mod.rs is 7.9k lines.

## Plan
- **One table per view** (model): each `View` knows its title, icon, go-to key and menu place in one `ViewSpec` table. The key bindings, the View menu (in table order, no indexes), the palette's go-to entries and the sidebar all read it. One `GoView(View)` action replaces GoInbox, GoTasks and the rest, if GPUI's actions allow a parameter; else one macro generates them from the table.
- **One icon map**: `kind_icon(Kind)` used by the kind slots, the views of a kind, group labels and the Agents rows; `view_icon` defers to it for kind views.
- **Configurable icon for declared kinds**: `[[kinds]] icon = "flag"`, checked against the app's icon names (an unknown one is a config error naming the choices); the CLI ignores it.
- **Shared form parts**: `ui/form.rs` with segmented, choice, toggle, chip, button and field, used by Settings and Agents; the copies go.
- **One duration format** in livtk-core (`format::duration`), used by the CLI and the app.
- **ui/mod.rs split along seams that exist**: rows and bands (`ui/list.rs`), the detail panel (`ui/detail.rs`), the sidebar (`ui/sidebar.rs`); no behaviour change.

## Acceptance check
- Adding a view is one table row plus its own drawing: a test lists every view and checks its key, menu item, palette entry and icon come from the table.
- One icon function per concept: a test checks each kind's slot icon equals its view's icon; a declared kind with `icon = "flag"` shows the flag; an unknown icon name stops with an error naming the choices.
- No duplicated helpers: settings.rs and agents.rs use ui/form.rs; one `duration` in core, tested.
- ui/mod.rs under 4k lines; every existing test passes unchanged except for moved paths; scripts/check passes.

data.title: Sessions in the log: every write from Claude names the session it came from
data.body:
From the human's word (2026-10-21): know in which Claude session each task was worked on, and by which agent, before livtk runs sessions itself (TAS-67).

## Findings this stands on
- Every Claude Code hook receives `session_id` and, for an agent, `agent_type` (FND-1). livtk's PreToolUse guard already rewrites the `livtk` commands Claude runs, to sign them with the agent's name.
- Events are read without `deny_unknown_fields`: an optional field is ignored by an older livtk, so no format bump.

## Plan
- An event may carry `session`: the Claude Code session id it was written from (optional; absent for the human and the app).
- The guard adds the session to every `livtk` command Claude runs (as it adds the agent), through a hidden `--session` flag the CLI also accepts from `LIVTK_SESSION`. A command typed by the human never has one.
- Core: `Workspace::sessions_of(KEY)`: the sessions that wrote to a node, each with its agent(s), first and last event; `Workspace::nodes_of_session(id)`: the nodes one session touched.
- CLI: `livtk show KEY` lists its sessions (id, agent, when); `livtk sessions [KEY]` lists sessions with the tasks they touched; `--json` both.

## Acceptance check
- A `livtk move` or `note` run by Claude through the hook writes an event with the session id and the agent; one run by the human writes none.
- `livtk show KEY` and `livtk sessions` list them; an older livtk reads the log unchanged (rows byte-identical with the field present).
- Tests in core, CLI and the hook; scripts/check passes.

data.title: Sessions in the Agents place: read past and live Claude sessions, and a task's sessions
data.body:
From the human's word (2026-10-21): a sessions view in Agents, to read the Claude sessions of this project, and from a task to the sessions that worked on it.

## Findings this stands on
- Claude Code keeps each session's transcript at `~/.claude/projects/<the folder, / and . as ->/<session-id>.jsonl` (one JSON record a line: user and assistant messages with tool calls, timestamps, `customTitle`, `agentName`, `isSidechain`), subagents' in a folder beside it. It deletes them after about 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays).

## Plan
- **Sessions**, in the Agents place (the live ones there today join this list): every session of this project, newest first, past and live, each with its title (its custom title, else its first prompt), when and how long, its agent, whether it is live (from `claude agents --json`), and the tasks it touched (from TAS-74's log).
- **Reading one**: the middle shows the conversation in order: your prompts, Claude's replies, each tool call folded to one line (opened on a click), subagents' work folded under the call that started them, compactions marked. Read off the window's thread and in pages, so a large transcript never stalls the app.
- **From a task**: its panel lists the sessions that worked on it (agent, when); a click opens the session at the first event it wrote for that task.
- A session whose transcript Claude Code no longer keeps still shows (from the log), saying its transcript is gone.
- Read-only: livtk never writes Claude Code's files.

- App tests (behaviour only); scripts/check passes.

data.body:
From the human's word (2026-10-21): a sessions view in Agents, to read the Claude sessions of this project, and from a task to the sessions that worked on it.

## Findings this stands on
- Claude Code keeps each session's transcript at `~/.claude/projects/<the folder, / and . as ->/<session-id>.jsonl` (one JSON record a line: user and assistant messages with tool calls, timestamps, `customTitle`, `agentName`, `isSidechain`), subagents' in a folder beside it. It deletes them after about 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays).

## Plan
- **Sessions**, in the Agents place (the live ones there today join this list): every session of this project, newest first, past and live, each with its title (its custom title, else its first prompt), when and how long, its agent, whether it is live (from `claude agents --json`), and the tasks it touched (from TAS-74's log).
- **Reading one**: the middle shows the conversation in order: your prompts, Claude's replies, each tool call folded to one line (opened on a click), subagents' work folded under the call that started them, compactions marked. Read off the window's thread and in pages, so a large transcript never stalls the app.
- **From a task** (the human's word on TAS-74, 2026-10-22): the session is part of the task's metadata, with its properties (Status, Priority, Created…): a **Session** row naming each session that worked on it (its title, agent, when), each one a link. A click opens that session in the Agents place, at the first event it wrote for this task, to review it.
- A session whose transcript Claude Code no longer keeps still shows (from the log), saying its transcript is gone.
- Read-only: livtk never writes Claude Code's files.

## Acceptance check
- With recorded transcripts (fixtures from real ones, trimmed): the list shows this project's sessions only, newest first, with title, agent, live state and tasks; opening one shows prompts, replies and folded tool calls in order; a subagent's work is under its call.
- A task's properties show its sessions (title, agent, when) and a click opens the right one, at that task's first event in it; a session without a transcript says so.
- A 50 MB transcript opens without stalling the window (paged).
- App tests (behaviour only); scripts/check passes.

data.text: Reply: noted on TAS-75, the task that builds the Sessions view: a task's properties get a Session row (each session that worked on it: its title, agent and when), and a click opens that session in Agents at the task's first event in it, so you can review it.
otherwise it looks all good and is very nice to see the sessions in the event logs
Reply: thank you. It is in review for you to mark done; that also lets TAS-75 (the Sessions view, with sessions in a task's properties) start once you ack it.

Built. Claude Code's files are read in one core module (livtk_core::claude), used by the app and by the CLI's claim (its own copy gone): the list reads only each transcript's first and last 256 KB (title, first prompt, start, end; this project's two, one 52 MB, list in 28 ms) and its subagents with the call that started each; a session reads a page of 200 entries from a byte offset (5 ms on the 52 MB one). Agents: Sessions is every session of the project, merged from the transcripts, Claude Code's live list and the log (agents, tasks touched), Needs you and running first, then by last activity. A session's panel: where it stands, when, its agents, the tasks it worked on, what it did in livtk (now exactly, from the log, not by time), Read, and while running Open and Stop; a session without a transcript says so. Read (or a double click) takes the list's place: prompts, replies, each call one line until opened with its input and result, compactions marked, a call that started a subagent offering its work (Esc back to the session), Read on for more; Esc back to the list. A task's properties have a Sessions row: each session (title, agents, when) opens it in Agents from the task's first event in it, marked. Tests: core (list with title, subagents, untitled names; paging adds up), app (sessions merged and ordered, Stop, a task's sessions opening the reader at its event, a call opened, a subagent's work and back, a session without a transcript). scripts/check passes.

review: REFUTED (2 of 4 points). (1) From a task, a click does not open the session in a fresh run: transcripts load only from the Agents place poll (ui/agents.rs:75-96, called from agents_view). go() (ui/mod.rs:1432) loads nothing, so read_session (model/agents.rs read_session) finds no transcript and warns "Claude Code no longer keeps this session's transcript" for a session that has one; the Sessions row also shows the short id, not the title. The test hides this by pressing "g e" first. (2) "At that task's first event" does not hold on real transcripts. Focus is the first entry with at >= the livtk event time. That is always the livtk call's tool_result (the tool_use is earlier), and reader_view skips Result entries ("Entry::Result => continue"), so no reader-focus mark is drawn. scroll_to_item(i) also uses the entry index, which runs ahead of the child index. Real case: the TAS-75 note at 20:52:55.717Z (call at 20:52:54.456Z), where the first entry at or after it is the tool_result at 20:54:46.625Z. The test passes only because its fixture has a reply dated 2999. (3) The list row shows the standing, name, a node count and when, but not the agent or which tasks (those are only in the panel). UPHELD: only this project's folder is listed, newest by last activity; prompts, replies, folded calls and compactions in order; a subagent's work is reached from its call; a session without a transcript says so (session-gone); listing reads 256 KB edges and the reader reads 200-entry pages off the main thread (the first page of the 52 MB one is fine). Titles: real custom-title records are re-appended near the end, so the tail read finds them. UNVERIFIABLE: no stall when the focus is deep in a 50 MB transcript. Every page up to the focus is read and rendered unvirtualized, and the whole reader is cloned on each render; settling it needs a timed run in the app. The 3 named tests pass. Also: the commit adds a test artifact, crates/livtk-app/.stub-stopped.

Build 219: Sessions is now its own view (G S), beside Agents under the Agents heading in the sidebar. Agents keeps only the agents. Sessions has the list (Needs you first), the panel (Read, Open, Stop, Worked on, What it did) and the reader. A session in a task's properties opens in Sessions, at that task's moment. Also fixed from the review: transcripts are found straight from a task; the mark lands on the call that wrote the event; long transcripts are read from just before that moment, with From the start; rows name their agents. Sorry for the mix-up, and thanks for the correction.

For TAS-77 (first event 20:02:40.882Z) and TAS-76 (20:02:40.894Z) in session c1c6d321, the real offset_near and read return a page whose first drawn entry is at 20:02:47.074Z. focus_index is None, so there is no reader-focus mark, and the call that wrote the event is not on the page. That covers the link groups in a task's panel (waits for, blocks, part of, sub-tasks, related, declared relations), a sub-task's parent chip in its row, and in Sessions, a session's 'Worked on' and 'What it did' lines. Build 224. What's in it:
- Runs are notes on the task, carrying the run's data (format 8): Started, Asks (a question, or the commands it was refused, each simple command apart), your Allowed/Denied, Ended (done, failed, stopped, quit). Rebuilt from the log, they give the same runs (tested).

- One idempotent settle turns finished turns into notes and starts the next turn once you've answered. The app runs it every 2s off the window's thread, and the CLI whenever it is asked about runs, or when you write a note.

Not in this task: worktree runs and merging (TAS-70), the Agent field and Start/Stop on a task, plus Allow/Deny buttons (TAS-69), and per-project allowed commands (TAS-70 settings). review: UPHELD core run loop: start/ask/inbox/allow/reply-resume/stop/continue all follow the stub stream-json (tests/run.rs 4/4, cli a_run_from_the_command_line, hooks 22/22 pass); run notes rebuild the same runs (run.rs:242); the writing mark lives only in .livtk/runs/writing (hooks test checks the log is unchanged); settle is under a lock and resumes once (pid guard); Allow/Deny refused for Claude in the CLI and in Command::RunNote. Before the first survey lands, or within 2s of a run started from the CLI, Cmd-Q quits without asking. data.title: The suggested agent on a task: shown first in the Agent field, from the task's stage and the agents' stage lines
data.body: Split from TAS-69 at the human's word. The Agent field in a task's detail offers the agent suggested for the stage the task is ready for: livtk's own for the stage (implementer to build, refuter to review), or an agent whose file says `stage: build` (the project's, then yours). It is shown first and marked as suggested, and taken in one click. The core already has the rule (livtk_core::run::suggest); this is the app's part.

data.text: Done as you said. The suggested agent is now its own task in the backlog: TAS-79. In TAS-69 the Agent field just lists every agent, with nothing marked as suggested. If a task has no agent chosen, Start runs livtk's own agent for the stage (the implementer to build, the refuter to review), as the CLI does. Starting now.

Build 227. A task's panel now has two new properties.
- Agent: pick any agent there is, or none, which means livtk's own for the stage. Nothing is suggested; that's TAS-79.
- Run: Start (to plan, build or review, as the task's state is ready for) shows 'Starting…' at once. Then it says where the run stands: writing, needs you, or going on, with Stop. After a run, it says how the last one ended.
The note a run waits on is marked Needs you. A permission gets Allow and Deny on that note. A question says 'Answer with a note below', and your note starts the next turn at once.
In the rows, 'Needs you' and 'Writing…' tags show. Sessions livtk didn't start also show as writing, on the in-progress tasks they worked on, via their hooks. Needs-you tasks come first in the Inbox.
Tested in the app with the stub, end to end without a terminal: pick the agent, Start, Needs you on the note and in the row, Allow, a question answered by a note, Writing… in the row, and Stop clearing it. The run tests now also kill any stub turn a failing test leaves behind.

review (refuter, 77cb3c1): UPHELD Start, needs-you answered in the app, run going on without a terminal: a_run_from_the_tasks_panel passes 7 of 8 runs alone (args(3) is '-p Blue. --resume', so a note in the app resumes the run via note -> survey_runs_soon -> settle -> resume). UPHELD Allow/Deny: shown only under the note whose id is the latest run's last_id while needs_you() (ui/runs.rs needs_you); not on a question (test asserts it); answer() refuses a question. UPHELD writing mark shows and clears with the turn, with the survey cadence (2s; a 'soon' asked while a survey is in flight is lost, so up to about 2s more). UPHELD Inbox: waiting runs first (workspace.rs inbox). UPHELD tests exist and test behaviour. Caveats, not refutations: (1) Flaky under load. 1 of 8 plain runs failed ('the runs never got there'); 1 of 3 under CPU load failed at ui.rs:4911 (set-agent-livtk:implementer not drawn yet: agents load late); 4 or 6 test processes at once fail every time at ui.rs:4959 (Stop does not end the stub turn: it loops until KillRuns). TAS-67's quitting_with_an_agent_working_asks_first fails the same way at ui.rs:4770, so this was there before this change. (2) ask_run (ui/runs.rs) does not check self.starting, and Runner::start checks for a running run without holding the lock, so two Start clicks dispatched before a redraw could start two runs. Allow has no pending state either, so a double click can write two Allowed notes or warn. Not reproduced. (3) Start shows even when claude cannot be found; clicking it only warns. No stub processes left behind.

Build 228 fixes the review's caveats.
- The flakiness had a real cause. A turn started by a program run in a shell script's background inherits SIGINT as ignored, and can't undo that, so Stop never reached it. Every parallel test run hit this. Now a turn still going 3 seconds after Stop gets SIGTERM, and SIGKILL at 8; the run is still noted as stopped and its work kept. Signals now go through the system call itself (rustix, no unsafe), and a failed ps counts as 'still running', not 'gone'. That also covers 'Stop skipped on a busy machine'.
- The core has a new test with a turn deaf to SIGINT: it is made to stop. 8 parallel runs of the five app run tests now pass, where every one failed before.
- Double clicks: the panel asks one thing of a task's run at a time, and the core starts a run under the runs' lock, so two Starts can't both start.
- Start is hidden, with the reason shown, when the claude command isn't found.
- The agent menu is waited for in the test, and the wait for runs has more headroom under load.
Started to review it, as livtk:refuter.
Stopped; the work so far is kept.

Proposed addition, from the first real run (the review of TAS-69): each project could have its own commands a run may always use, per stage, in the project's settings, for example 'cargo test *' for reviews and builds. Today a run may only read files and use livtk, plus edit them in a build, so a review that runs the tests stops on Allow every time. Say if you want it in this task; otherwise I'll leave it out.

There could be several updates I think in terms of experience, for example metadata name is actually vertically centered which instead should align top and the content of it should by default be like that.

another thing is that the livtk's own for the stage should be named "Default"

run button should be placed in the task's details titlebar where the id of it is written but the run button should just be like it is right now and be placed right after the task id

data.title: Task panel polish: properties aligned to the top, the Default agent, the run in the title bar
data.body:
From the human's note on TAS-69.

## Plan
- Properties: each row's name sits at the top of its row, not centred against a tall value, and values align to the top by default. One change in the shared prop_row, so every property follows.
- The Agent field's 'livtk's own for the stage' is called **Default**, on the button and in its menu.
- The run (its status, Start or Stop) moves from the properties into the panel's title bar, right after the task's key, as it looks now. The Run property row goes away.

## Acceptance check
- A property whose value spans lines keeps its name at the top.
- The agent button and menu say Default when no agent is picked.
- Start/Stop and the run's status show in the title bar after the key, and work as before. The app's run test passes with the run in its new place.
